NCC Promotion Exam - Controlled Teaching Expansion v4.0 - Checkpoint 2   Page 151  DEEP CHAPTER 11 - WHAT SPECTRUM ACTUALLY IS  11.1 Begin with electromagnetic energy  Wireless communication works by using electromagnetic waves to carry information through space. A transmitter generates a controlled signal; an antenna radiates it; the wave travels through the environment; a receiving antenna captures part of the energy; and the receiver interprets the signal. Radio-frequency spectrum is the range of frequencies used for radio communication and related services.  Frequency tells us how many wave cycles occur each second. The unit is the hertz. One kilohertz is one thousand hertz; one megahertz is one million; one gigahertz is one billion. Wavelength is the physical distance covered by one cycle. In free space, higher frequency corresponds to shorter wavelength.  11.2 Why the spectrum is not consumed like fuel  A transmission does not permanently use up a frequency. Spectrum is reusable across time, geography, power levels and technical arrangements. The scarcity arises because simultaneous uses can conflict, useful propagation differs by band, equipment ecosystems concentrate around particular bands, and interference must be controlled. It is therefore scarce in an economic and regulatory sense.  11.3 Spectrum is a national resource, not operator property  An assignment gives defined rights of use under conditions; it does not transfer sovereign ownership of the electromagnetic spectrum. Conditions may specify geography, band, bandwidth, power, technology neutrality or restriction, duration, fees, rollout and interference obligations.  EXAM TRAP - Spectrum is not a physical substance stored inside a licence. A licence or assignment creates conditional authority to use frequencies; the resource remains subject to public-interest management.

NCC Promotion Exam - Controlled Teaching Expansion v4.0 - Checkpoint 2   Page 152  DEEP CHAPTER 12 - FREQUENCY, WAVELENGTH AND PROPAGATION  12.1 The central trade-off  LOWER FREQUENCY  Wider reach / stronger penetration  MID-BAND  Coverage-capacity balance  HIGHER FREQUENCY  More bandwidth / shorter reach  General tendency only: actual performance also depends on power, bandwidth, antennas, terrain, buildings and network design.  Lower-frequency signals generally travel farther and penetrate obstacles better than higher-frequency signals under comparable conditions. Higher-frequency bands can offer wider contiguous bandwidth but commonly require denser infrastructure because propagation and penetration are more demanding. This is a tendency, not a guarantee.  12.2 What propagation includes  Effect   Plain-English explanation   Network consequence  Path loss   Signal energy weakens with distance and environment.   Limits cell reach and link budget.  Reflection   Signal bounces from surfaces.   Can extend or distort paths.  Diffraction   Wave bends around an obstacle or edge.   Helps some coverage beyond direct sight.  Scattering   Energy disperses from rough surfaces or small objects.   Creates multiple weak paths.  Absorption   Materials take up signal energy.   Walls, foliage and rain can reduce signal.  Multipath   Copies arrive by different routes and times.   Can cause fading; modern systems can also exploit it.  12.3 Link budget thinking  A link budget accounts for transmitted power, antenna gains, cable and connector losses, propagation loss, receiver sensitivity and a margin for fading and uncertainty. The point is not to memorise one formula: it is to recognise that usable coverage depends on the whole radio path, not frequency alone.  LEVEL 10 INSIGHT - When comparing bands, state both the physical tendency and the engineering context. Avoid absolute claims such as '700 MHz always has better service' or '3.5 GHz is only for cities.'

NCC Promotion Exam - Controlled Teaching Expansion v4.0 - Checkpoint 2   Page 153  DEEP CHAPTER 13 - BANDWIDTH, CAPACITY AND SPECTRAL EFFICIENCY  13.1 Frequency is a position; bandwidth is a span  A centre frequency identifies where a channel sits. Bandwidth describes the width of spectrum occupied or authorised. A 100 MHz block offers a wider frequency span than a 20 MHz block. Wider bandwidth can support more data, but delivered capacity also depends on signal quality, technology, antennas, scheduling, interference, backhaul and user demand.  13.2 Spectral efficiency  Spectral efficiency describes how effectively information is carried per unit of bandwidth. Newer modulation, coding and multiple-antenna techniques can increase efficiency when radio conditions permit. Efficiency is not limitless: robust transmission under weak or noisy conditions may carry fewer information bits than aggressive transmission under clean conditions.  13.3 Capacity has several dimensions  Capacity lever   How it helps   Constraint  More bandwidth   Provides more radio resource.   Scarcity, cost and availability.  Better spectral efficiency   Carries more useful data per hertz.   Needs suitable signal quality and equipment.  More cells / sectorisation   Reuses spectrum across smaller areas.   Sites, power, backhaul, interference and cost.  Traffic offload   Moves suitable traffic to Wi-Fi or other systems.   Coverage, security and user/device support.  Demand management   Balances or prioritises traffic.   Transparency, neutrality, consumer and licence issues.  13.4 Contiguous and fragmented holdings  A large contiguous block is often easier to use efficiently than the same total bandwidth split into separated fragments. Carrier aggregation can combine supported carriers, but device capability, band combinations and deployment complexity matter.  EXAM TRAP - More spectrum can increase potential capacity; it does not automatically guarantee faster service. The end-to-end network must convert the radio resource into usable performance.

NCC Promotion Exam - Controlled Teaching Expansion v4.0 - Checkpoint 2   Page 154  DEEP CHAPTER 14 - CHANNELS, DUPLEXING AND MULTIPLE ACCESS  14.1 Separating users and directions  A network must organise many simultaneous communications. It divides resources by frequency, time, code, subcarrier, space or combinations of these. The engineering objective is controlled sharing: users should communicate without unacceptable mutual interference.  14.2 Frequency Division Duplex and Time Division Duplex  Method   How uplink and downlink are separated   Regulatory/engineering significance  Frequency Division Duplex (FDD)   Uses paired frequency blocks: one for uplink and another for downlink.  Needs suitable paired spectrum and separation; useful where traffic balance and ecosystem support fit.  Time Division Duplex (TDD)   Uses the same frequency block at different times for uplink and downlink.  Can adjust time balance but requires synchronisation and interference coordination.  Uplink is transmission from user equipment toward the network. Downlink is transmission from the network toward the user. Consumer traffic is often downlink-heavy, but applications such as video contribution, cloud backup and industrial systems can increase uplink demand.  14.3 Guard bands and emission limits  Adjacent services may need separation, filters, guard bands or emission masks so energy from one assignment does not cause harmful interference to another. A guard band improves coexistence but also represents spectrum that may not carry ordinary user traffic. Efficient management therefore balances utilisation and protection.  14.4 Licensed, licence-exempt and shared use  Exclusive licensed access can provide predictable rights and investment certainty. Licence-exempt use permits compliant equipment under general conditions, as in common Wi-Fi bands. Shared arrangements allow multiple users under defined coordination, geography, power or database rules. Licence-exempt does not mean rule-free, interference-free or owned by the user.  EXAM TRAP - TDD is not the same as unpaired spectrum in every context, and FDD is not simply 'two networks.' They are duplex arrangements for separating transmission directions.

NCC Promotion Exam - Controlled Teaching Expansion v4.0 - Checkpoint 2   Page 155  DEEP CHAPTER 15 - INTERFERENCE: THE CENTRAL MANAGEMENT PROBLEM  15.1 Not every unwanted signal is legally harmful interference  Interference is unwanted radio energy that degrades reception. Whether it is harmful depends on the affected service, severity, persistence and applicable definitions. Regulators must distinguish a weak wanted signal, equipment fault, congestion and actual external interference.  15.2 Main interference patterns  Pattern   Cause   Control approach  Co-channel   Same or reused frequency reaches the victim receiver too strongly.  Geographic separation, power, antenna and coordination.  Adjacent-channel   Energy spills or receiver selectivity allows a nearby channel to interfere.  Emission limits, filters, guard bands and compliant equipment.  Cross-border   Transmission in one country affects a service in another.  Bilateral, regional and ITU-aligned coordination.  Intermodulation / unwanted products  Equipment non-linearity combines signals into new components.  Engineering correction, filtering and site discipline.  Illegal or unauthorised use   Transmitter operates without authority or outside conditions.  Monitoring, investigation and enforcement.  15.3 The interference-investigation chain  •   Confirm the complaint: service, frequency, place, time, equipment and effect.  •   Measure and characterise the signal using calibrated monitoring tools.  •   Locate or narrow the source through fixed, mobile or direction-finding methods.  •   Check assignments, technical parameters, equipment approval and licence conditions.  •   Engage affected parties, require corrective action and apply enforcement where justified.  •   Re-measure to verify that the harmful condition has ended.  REGULATORY PRINCIPLE - A spectrum monitor detects energy, not guilt. Attribution requires technical evidence, authority records, equipment checks and due process.

NCC Promotion Exam - Controlled Teaching Expansion v4.0 - Checkpoint 2   Page 156  DEEP CHAPTER 16 - ALLOCATION, ALLOTMENT, ASSIGNMENT AND LICENSING  16.1 The hierarchy  Level   Question answered   Example form  International allocation   Which radio services may use a band within the global/regional framework?  Mobile, fixed, broadcasting, satellite or other service allocation.  National allocation   How does Nigeria designate bands in its National Frequency Allocation Table?  National primary/secondary use and footnotes.  Allotment   How is a frequency channel or block entered in a plan for an area or service?  Common in planned services; distinct from a station assignment.  Assignment   Which eligible station, user or licensee may use a specified frequency under conditions?  A defined block, channel, geography, power and term.  Licence/authorisation   What legal permission and obligations govern the activity or resource use?  Spectrum licence and, where required, service/facility licence.  16.2 Service licence versus spectrum authorisation  A service licence permits a communications service or facility within its scope. A spectrum authorisation permits defined use of frequency resources. Some activities need both; others use licence-exempt bands subject to general rules; some licensees, such as an MVNO under the applicable framework, may provide services without owning spectrum assignments.  16.3 Primary and secondary allocations  Where the table distinguishes primary and secondary services, secondary use ordinarily operates with reduced protection: it must not cause harmful interference to primary services and cannot claim protection from compliant primary use, subject to the governing footnotes and Radio Regulations.  EXAM TRAP - Allocation designates a band for a category of radio service. Assignment authorises a particular use. Neither word should be used casually to mean an auction result, service licence or completed network rollout.

NCC Promotion Exam - Controlled Teaching Expansion v4.0 - Checkpoint 2   Page 157  DEEP CHAPTER 17 - WHO DOES WHAT IN NIGERIA  17.1 Institutional architecture  The Nigerian Communications Act creates a relationship among national policy, the Minister, the National Frequency Management Council and the Commission. The Council is part of the national frequency-management architecture, while NCC manages and administers spectrum for the communications sector within the statutory and national planning framework. International obligations and coordination remain relevant because radio waves and satellite systems do not respect borders.  Actor   Core spectrum role   Do not misstate as  International Telecommunication Union / WRC process  Maintains and revises the international Radio Regulations and allocation framework through Member State processes.  A body that assigns Nigerian mobile frequencies directly to operators.  Federal policy / national frequency architecture  Sets national direction and coordinates national allocation across sectors and uses.  An operator licensing department.  National Frequency Management Council  Performs statutory national frequency-planning and coordination functions under the Act.  The same institution as NCC.  NCC   Plans, licenses, assigns, prices, monitors and enforces communications-sector spectrum use within its mandate.  Owner of every frequency used by all government sectors.  Licensee/user   Uses assigned or permitted spectrum under conditions and must manage emissions/interference.  Permanent owner free from regulatory control.  17.2 Why international coordination matters  Cross-border terrestrial systems can interfere. Satellite networks depend on internationally coordinated orbital and frequency records. Equipment markets benefit from harmonised bands. Nigeria therefore makes national decisions within a wider international and regional environment while retaining sovereign regulatory authority.  LEVEL 10 INSIGHT - Institutional accuracy is part of technical accuracy. Before recommending action, identify whether the issue concerns international allocation, national planning, communications-sector assignment, licensee compliance or cross-border coordination.

NCC Promotion Exam - Controlled Teaching Expansion v4.0 - Checkpoint 2   Page 158  DEEP CHAPTER 18 - THE SPECTRUM-MANAGEMENT LIFECYCLE  18.1 From public need to verified use  •   Forecast demand: technology, market, public-service, security and inclusion needs.  •   Plan the band: international allocation, national table, incumbents, coexistence and equipment ecosystem.  •   Consult where required: publish questions or proposals and obtain stakeholder evidence.  •   Choose an access method: administrative assignment, auction, beauty contest, first-come process, licence-exempt or sharing framework as law and policy allow.  •   Authorise and price: define rights, fees, coverage, rollout, technical, reporting and interference conditions.  •   Coordinate and clear: manage incumbents, migration, cross-border use and equipment readiness.  •   Monitor deployment and utilisation: distinguish possession from effective use.  •   Enforce conditions and resolve interference.  •   Review, renew, trade, refarm, recover or reassign according to the operative framework and public interest.  18.2 Why spectrum pricing exists  Pricing can recover administrative costs, reflect scarcity, promote efficient use and support transparent competitive selection. But maximising upfront revenue is not the only public objective. Excessive cost can constrain investment; weak conditions can encourage warehousing; poorly designed awards can damage competition.  18.3 Utilisation  A licence holder may possess an assignment yet under-deploy it. Efficient-utilisation assessment can consider actual network deployment, traffic, geography, technology, rollout milestones and whether the band can serve public objectives more effectively. Utilisation is not proved merely by paying a fee.  EXAM TRAP - Spectrum management does not end at assignment. Monitoring, coordination, compliance, renewal and refarming are equally part of the lifecycle.

NCC Promotion Exam - Controlled Teaching Expansion v4.0 - Checkpoint 2   Page 159  DEEP CHAPTER 19 - AUCTIONS AND OTHER ASSIGNMENT METHODS  19.1 Why auction  Where demand exceeds available spectrum, an auction can identify bidders willing and able to pay for defined rights through a transparent competitive process. A well-designed auction specifies eligibility, lots, reserve price, bidding rules, deposits, competition safeguards, payment, licence conditions and default consequences.  19.2 The Nigerian 3.5 GHz example  The NCC's final Information Memorandum for the 2021 3.5 GHz auction offered two lots of 100 MHz time-division-duplex spectrum to deepen broadband and support fifth-generation deployment. The document is evidence of the award design and historical auction process; it should not be used as proof that every subsequent deployment milestone or coverage claim was achieved.  Method   Strength   Risk requiring control  Auction   Transparent price discovery where demand is competitive.  Winner's curse, concentration, strategic bidding or excessive cost.  Administrative assignment   Can fit specialised, local, public-interest or low-demand cases.  Needs clear criteria and non-discrimination.  Comparative selection   Can weigh technical and rollout commitments.   Subjective scoring must be controlled and auditable.  Licence-exempt/general authorisation  Supports innovation and low barriers for compliant devices.  Congestion and limited interference protection.  Sharing framework   Can increase utilisation and accommodate multiple uses.  Coordination complexity and uncertain responsibility.  19.3 Award is not deployment  The sequence is proposal or consultation, final rules or memorandum, bidding, provisional outcome, payment and compliance, licence/assignment, rollout and ongoing monitoring. Each stage has a different status. Examination answers should use the correct verb: proposed, consulted, auctioned, awarded, licensed, deployed or achieved.  EXAM TRAP - An auction is an assignment mechanism, not the spectrum itself; a winning bid is not automatically nationwide service; and an information memorandum is not a general regulation.

NCC Promotion Exam - Controlled Teaching Expansion v4.0 - Checkpoint 2   Page 160  DEEP CHAPTER 20 - REFARMING, TRADING, SHARING AND RECOVERY  20.1 Refarming  Refarming reorganises or redeploys a band for a different technology or service arrangement. It may move incumbents, change channel plans or permit newer technology. The policy case can include efficiency and better services; the implementation problem includes continuity, equipment replacement, interference, consumer migration, compensation and timing.  20.2 Spectrum trading  Trading allows rights to move between eligible parties under an approved framework. It can put underused spectrum into more productive hands, but it requires prior regulatory review of eligibility, competition, technical conditions, liabilities and the integrity of the assignment register. A private commercial agreement alone does not necessarily complete a lawful transfer.  20.3 Spectrum sharing  Form   How it works   Key concern  Geographic sharing   Different users operate in separated areas.   Boundary interference and coordination.  Time sharing   Users access the band at different times.   Scheduling, predictability and priority.  Power/technical sharing   Users coexist under emission, antenna or power constraints.  Monitoring and receiver protection.  Dynamic/database-assisted sharing   Access decisions respond to incumbent records or detected availability.  Database accuracy, enforcement and security.  20.4 Recovery and renewal  Assignments have terms and conditions. Renewal should not be assumed as perpetual ownership. Depending on law and the instrument, NCC may assess compliance, utilisation, fees, interference and public interest. Recovery or non-renewal requires lawful process and attention to continuity and legitimate expectations.  LEVEL 10 BALANCE - Refarming, trading and sharing can increase efficiency, but each can affect investment certainty, competition, incumbents and consumers. A strong answer names both benefit and safeguard.

NCC Promotion Exam - Controlled Teaching Expansion v4.0 - Checkpoint 2   Page 161  DEEP CHAPTER 21 - SATELLITE, ORBITS AND NON-TERRESTRIAL NETWORKS  21.1 Frequency and orbit are connected resources  Satellite communication needs suitable frequency bands and an orbital configuration. Geostationary satellites appear fixed relative to Earth and can cover wide areas with a small number of spacecraft, but the long path adds latency. Low-Earth-orbit constellations reduce path length and can support lower latency, but require many moving satellites, tracking, handover and complex coordination.  21.2 Filing does not equal ownership  International satellite coordination uses the ITU Radio Regulations and filing processes. A filing records and coordinates a network within defined procedures; it does not grant a state or company unrestricted ownership of outer space. National landing rights, gateways, service licensing, equipment and security requirements can still apply.  21.3 Direct-to-device  Direct-to-device satellite systems seek to communicate with ordinary or adapted user devices without conventional terrestrial coverage at that location. Regulatory questions include band compatibility, protection of terrestrial networks, emergency use, roaming and numbering, gateway location, lawful access, consumer terms, service quality and cross-border provision.  The NCC's January 2026 direct-to-device consultation was explicitly consultation-stage: it was not itself a licensing process, spectrum assignment or final regulatory decision. This makes it an excellent status-classification example.  21.4 Gateway and feeder links  A user link connects the satellite to the subscriber terminal; feeder links connect a satellite system to gateway earth stations and terrestrial networks. A satellite service can therefore depend on terrestrial fibre, data centres, interconnection and power as well as the space segment.  EXAM TRAP - Non-terrestrial network is the umbrella concept. Low-Earth-orbit satellite, high-altitude platform and direct-to-device service are related examples or implementations, not exact synonyms.

NCC Promotion Exam - Controlled Teaching Expansion v4.0 - Checkpoint 2   Page 162  DEEP CHAPTER 22 - SPECTRUM MONITORING AND ENFORCEMENT  22.1 What monitoring seeks to know  •   Is the assigned frequency being used, and by whom?  •   Does the signal stay within authorised frequency, bandwidth, geography, power and emission conditions?  •   Is the assignment being used efficiently and consistently with rollout obligations?  •   Is harmful interference occurring, and what is its source?  •   Are unlicensed or non-compliant transmitters operating?  •   Do monitoring records support planning, coordination and enforcement decisions?  22.2 Tools and evidence  Fixed monitoring stations provide continuing observation. Mobile units investigate locations and routes. Spectrum analysers show energy across frequency. Direction-finding systems help locate emitters. Drive tests and network measurements can connect radio conditions to service performance. Equipment calibration, time, location, antenna configuration and chain of custody affect evidential reliability.  22.3 Compliance response  A proportionate response may begin with notification or technical coordination where an accidental configuration or faulty device is involved. Persistent unauthorised use, deliberate non-compliance or harmful interference can justify stronger enforcement. The Commission should connect the measured conduct to the applicable assignment, licence, regulation or statutory power and preserve procedural fairness.  22.4 Monitoring versus Quality of Service testing  Spectrum monitoring examines radio use and emissions. Quality of Service testing examines delivered service performance under a defined methodology. They can inform each other but are not interchangeable: a clean spectrum observation does not prove adequate service capacity, and a slow speed test does not by itself prove external interference.  LEVEL 10 INSIGHT - Monitoring becomes regulation only when measurement is converted into reliable attribution, legal classification, proportionate action and verified correction.

NCC Promotion Exam - Controlled Teaching Expansion v4.0 - Checkpoint 2   Page 163  LEVEL 10 SPECTRUM APPLICATION DRILLS  Scenario 1 - Rural coverage obligation  An operator asks for additional low-band spectrum, arguing that it will improve rural coverage. How should NCC assess the request?  MODEL REASONING  Lower-band propagation can improve reach and building penetration, but the claim should be tested against resource availability, national allocation, existing holdings and utilisation, competition effects, rollout commitments, infrastructure and backhaul plans, device ecosystem, fees and interference coordination. NCC should define measurable geographic or population obligations, milestones, reporting and consequences. The decision must connect public benefit to enforceable use, rather than assume that assignment alone creates coverage.  Scenario 2 - Adjacent-band complaint  A satellite earth station reports interference after a new terrestrial network begins operation nearby.  •   Confirm the victim service, authorised parameters, frequency, time and effect.  •   Measure wanted and unwanted signals and distinguish overload, equipment fault and external emission.  •   Check allocation footnotes, assignment priority, coordination obligations and emission limits.  •   Examine transmitter configuration, antenna orientation, filtering and receiver characteristics.  •   Coordinate corrective action and verify through re-measurement; enforce if breach is established.  Scenario 3 - Winning bidder delays rollout  NCC should distinguish financial completion from substantive utilisation. It should review the information memorandum, licence and rollout milestones; verify deployment and coverage evidence; consider causes, competition and consumer impact; and apply the authorised remedy. The objective is not punishment for its own sake but credible conditions, efficient use and public value.  Scenario 4 - Private spectrum sale  Two companies announce that one has bought the other's frequencies. A commercial agreement does not by itself prove regulatory transfer. NCC should verify whether trading is permitted, prior approval was obtained, the buyer is eligible, competition and technical conditions remain acceptable, fees and liabilities are resolved, and the official assignment register has been updated.

NCC Promotion Exam - Controlled Teaching Expansion v4.0 - Checkpoint 2   Page 164  SPECTRUM EXAM TRAPS AND RAPID RECALL  Trap   Correct position  Spectrum is exhausted when transmitted.   It is reusable; scarcity comes from interference, propagation, demand and coordination constraints.  Higher frequency always means faster Internet.   Higher bands may offer bandwidth, but coverage and performance depend on the full network.  Bandwidth and frequency are the same.   Frequency locates a signal; bandwidth is the span occupied or authorised.  Allocation equals assignment.   Allocation designates a band for a service; assignment authorises a particular use.  A service licence automatically includes spectrum.  Service and spectrum authorisations are distinct even where both are required.  An auction is the only fair method.   Method depends on scarcity and objectives; transparency and non-discrimination apply to all.  Winning spectrum means 5G achievement.   Award, licensing, deployment, adoption and service outcome are separate stages.  Licence-exempt means unregulated.   General technical and equipment rules still apply, with limited interference protection.  Trading is an ordinary private sale.   Transfer remains subject to the regulatory framework and approval.  A roadmap proves implementation.   A roadmap expresses planned direction; completed action needs separate evidence.  THE 20-SECOND SPECTRUM ANSWER  Spectrum is the regulated frequency resource that enables wireless services. International and national allocation determine permissible service uses; NCC assigns and licenses communications-sector use under conditions; licensees deploy networks; monitoring checks utilisation and interference; and renewal, trading, refarming, sharing or recovery keep the resource aligned with competition, investment, coverage, innovation and consumer welfare.  SELF-CHECK  •   Can I explain frequency, wavelength and bandwidth without hiding behind symbols?  •   Can I compare low, mid and high bands without making absolute claims?  •   Can I distinguish allocation, allotment, assignment, auction and licence?  •   Can I explain why spectrum assignment does not guarantee coverage or quality?  •   Can I classify roadmap, consultation, auction outcome, licence and deployment correctly?  •   Can I turn an interference complaint into an evidence and enforcement sequence?

NCC Promotion Exam - Controlled Teaching Expansion v4.0 - Checkpoint 3   Page 167  DEEP CHAPTER 23 - WHY COMMUNICATIONS ARE LICENSED  23.1 A licence is structured permission  A communications licence is a legal authorisation to undertake a defined activity subject to scope, duration, obligations and regulatory oversight. It is not merely a certificate proving that a fee was paid. The licence converts an otherwise prohibited regulated activity into a permitted one, but only within the authority granted.  Licensing allows NCC to control market entry, identify accountable providers, attach technical and consumer obligations, manage scarce resources, support competition, collect information and intervene when conduct threatens the statutory objectives.  23.2 Section 31: the basic prohibition  Section 31(1) of the Nigerian Communications Act 2003 states the central rule: no person may operate a communications system or facility or provide a communications service in Nigeria unless authorised under a communications licence or exempted under regulations made by the Commission.  The statutory wording covers three ideas that should not be collapsed: operating a communications system, operating a communications facility, and providing a communications service. Whether a business model falls within one or more categories depends on what it actually does, not merely how it describes itself.  23.3 Why exemption is not absence of law  An exempt activity is outside the requirement to obtain a licence only because the Commission has lawfully exempted it under regulations. Exemption may still carry equipment, interference, consumer, security or general legal requirements. A company cannot create its own exemption by asserting that its service is small or Internet-based.  EXAM TRAP - 'Unlicensed' can mean unlawful operation without authority; 'licence-exempt' means operation permitted without an individual or class registration under a lawful regulatory exemption. They are opposites, not synonyms.

NCC Promotion Exam - Controlled Teaching Expansion v4.0 - Checkpoint 3   Page 168  DEEP CHAPTER 24 - OFFENCE AND CONSEQUENCES  24.1 The statutory consequence  A person who breaches section 31(1) commits an offence. On conviction, section 31(2) provides for a fine not less than the initial fee for the relevant licence and not exceeding ten times that initial fee, imprisonment for a term not exceeding one year, or both. The proviso also addresses forfeiture to the Commission of property, facilities, installations and equipment used for the unlicensed service.  The Act's criminal consequence must be distinguished from administrative fines or enforcement measures created by subsidiary legislation. An examination question may test whether a quoted figure comes from the Act, a regulation, a licence condition or a later enforcement framework.  24.2 The regulator still needs classification evidence  Before alleging unlicensed operation, NCC must understand the service architecture, provider role, customer relationship, facilities used, territorial connection and any applicable exemption. A website, application or marketing label may hide several underlying regulated roles.  Evidence question   Why it matters  What service is actually supplied?   Determines whether the activity is within a licensed category.  Who contracts with and bills the customer?   Helps identify the provider and commercial responsibility.  Who owns or controls network facilities?   Separates reseller, infrastructure, platform and network roles.  Is spectrum or numbering used?   May trigger additional resource authorisation.  Where is the service provided or used?   Connects the activity to the Act's territorial scope.  Is there an exemption or class licence?   Prevents misclassifying lawful general-authorisation activity.  24.3 Enforcement is not merely punishment  The regulatory objective includes stopping unlawful service, protecting consumers, preserving network integrity and restoring lawful competition. NCC may need a transition plan where abrupt closure would strand customers or disrupt essential connectivity, while still applying the available legal consequences.  LEVEL 10 INSIGHT - First classify the activity and legal requirement; then prove the conduct; then select the lawful and proportionate response. Do not begin with the penalty and work backwards.

NCC Promotion Exam - Controlled Teaching Expansion v4.0 - Checkpoint 3   Page 169  DEEP CHAPTER 25 - CLASS AND INDIVIDUAL LICENCES  25.1 Section 32 creates the two licensing forms  NCC issues communications licences by way of class or individual licences on terms and conditions it determines, taking account of the Act's objectives and the principles in section 33(3). The Commission determines and publishes which services qualify for each category or are exempt.  Feature   Individual licence   Class licence  Regulatory design   Specific authorisation granted to a named licensee.   General licence with standard conditions for a defined class of activity.  Entry mechanism   Written application, assessment and grant under sections 39-42 or a competitive process.  Registration notice and prescribed registration fee under section 50.  Conditions   General, service-specific and special/additional conditions may apply.  Standard conditions apply to registered persons in the class.  Typical regulatory intensity   Usually higher where infrastructure, scarcity, market power, public risk or complex obligations exist.  Usually lower where common conditions can govern multiple similar providers.  Exit/enforcement language   Renewal, surrender, suspension and revocation under sections 43-47.  De-registration under section 51.  25.2 A class licence is not a lower-quality licence  The classification reflects how the activity can be regulated, not whether the provider is important. Class licensing reduces individual transaction cost by applying standard conditions. Registration remains a condition precedent, subject to the Act's exceptions.  25.3 Protecting existing holders  Section 32(3) requires NCC, when determining which services qualify for class or individual licensing, to ensure that previous holders are not disadvantaged except as permitted under the Act and subsidiary legislation. This introduces transition fairness when categories change.  EXAM TRAP - 'Class licence' does not mean a licence issued to a classroom or a collective company. It is a general authorisation framework with common conditions; each intending operator must still register as required.

NCC Promotion Exam - Controlled Teaching Expansion v4.0 - Checkpoint 3   Page 170  DEEP CHAPTER 26 - SECTION 33: PROCESS AND PRINCIPLES  26.1 Procedure is not improvised for each applicant  Section 33 requires NCC to publish regulation on its licensing processes, including general eligibility, and to determine and publish procedures. Permitted methods may include auction, selection processes, public tender invitation or competitive bidding. The list is not exhaustive.  26.2 The six-part decision discipline  Section 33(3) principle   What it demands in practice  Transparency, fairness and non-discrimination   Published criteria, consistent treatment, reasons and auditable decisions.  Efficient radio-frequency management   Licensing must not create unusable, conflicting or wasteful spectrum rights.  Available numbers under the National Numbering Plan   A service requiring numbers cannot assume unlimited numbering resources.  Fair competition and investment   Entry design should deter foreclosure while sustaining credible investment.  Modern, qualitative, affordable and readily available services nationwide  Licensing should translate into consumer and national-development outcomes.  Other necessary national-interest considerations   Allows adaptation, but not arbitrary action detached from statutory purpose.  26.3 Equal treatment does not always mean identical treatment  Non-discrimination requires comparable cases to be treated consistently and material differences to be treated on relevant grounds. A nationwide spectrum-dependent network and a small licence-exempt local device may legitimately face different rules. The difference must connect to lawful objectives.  26.4 The correct verbs  A consultation invites evidence. A public tender invites qualifying offers. An auction applies bidding rules. Selection evaluates stated criteria. A licence grant authorises activity. Deployment implements the right. Commercial launch offers service. Achievement requires verified outcome. These stages should never be compressed into 'NCC approved it.'  LEVEL 10 INSIGHT - Section 33(3) is not decorative language. It is a decision-quality test for procedures, licence grants and licence conditions.

NCC Promotion Exam - Controlled Teaching Expansion v4.0 - Checkpoint 3   Page 171  DEEP CHAPTER 27 - LICENCE CONDITIONS AND DECLARATIONS  27.1 The licence is the authority; conditions define its boundaries  A licence answers whether the licensee may conduct the regulated activity. Conditions answer how, where, for how long and subject to what obligations. Conditions can cover service scope, territory, rollout, quality, consumer protection, fees, reporting, technical standards, spectrum, numbering, interconnection, security, ownership changes and compliance.  27.2 Sections 34-37: declarations and procedural safeguards  •   Section 34 permits written declarations that an individual licence, a classification of individual licences or a class licence is subject to terms and conditions or enjoys specified benefits.  •   The declaration must be consistent with the objects and relevant provisions of the Act.  •   Before making it, section 35 requires written notice to affected licensees and a draft declaration.  •   Affected licensees must receive at least 30 days to make written submissions.  •   NCC must consider submissions and section 33(3) principles.  •   Section 36 requires registration of declarations.  •   Section 37 permits amendment, modification, variation or revocation, using the same procedures as applicable.  27.3 General, specific and additional conditions  General conditions can apply widely across licensees. Service-specific conditions respond to the characteristics of a licence category. Special or additional conditions respond to a particular grant, competitive process or licensee situation. A candidate should identify the source before asserting that every licensee has the same obligation.  EXAM TRAP - A licence condition is not the licence itself. Breach of a condition may trigger regulatory consequences, but it does not mean the original authorisation never existed.

NCC Promotion Exam - Controlled Teaching Expansion v4.0 - Checkpoint 3   Page 172  DEEP CHAPTER 28 - PERSONAL NATURE, TRANSFER AND CONTROL  28.1 Section 38  The grant is personal to the licensee. It may not be operated by, assigned, sub-licensed or transferred to another party without NCC's prior written approval. The licensee must always comply with its licence, the Act and subsidiary legislation.  28.2 Why prior approval matters  NCC assessed a particular legal entity, ownership structure, competence, financial capacity and competitive position. An uncontrolled transfer could place the authorisation in the hands of an ineligible party, concentrate the market, separate the licence from its obligations or frustrate enforcement.  Transaction   Regulatory question  Share acquisition or change of control   Does the licence or applicable rule require prior approval, notification or competition review?  Asset sale   Are network assets moving while the licence remains with the seller? Who serves customers?  Outsourcing   Is a contractor performing tasks for the licensee, or unlawfully operating the licensed activity in its own right?  Sub-licensing arrangement   Is the licensee attempting to confer regulatory rights it cannot transfer privately?  Merger or restructuring   Will the surviving entity hold the authority, resources and obligations lawfully?  28.3 Outsourcing does not outsource accountability  A licensee may engage vendors where permitted, but remains accountable for compliance unless the framework says otherwise. Managed services, cloud hosting, tower sharing and agents do not automatically become licensees; equally, contractual labels cannot conceal an unauthorised provider.  LEVEL 10 INSIGHT - Analyse substance: who controls the service, network, customers and regulatory decisions? Then check the specific licence and approval rules.

NCC Promotion Exam - Controlled Teaching Expansion v4.0 - Checkpoint 3   Page 173  DEEP CHAPTER 29 - APPLYING FOR AN INDIVIDUAL LICENCE  29.1 Sections 39-42  NEED   ELIGIBILITY   APPLICATION   DECISION   COMPLIANCE  Licensing is a lifecycle: authorisation is followed by operation, monitoring, renewal and possible exit.  A person applies in writing and in NCC's prescribed form. NCC may specify additional criteria and qualifications. An applicant already operating under a class licence for the same service or activity cannot be granted an individual licence for that same activity under section 39(3). Processing fees apply, and the application may be withdrawn before grant or refusal.  29.2 Completeness is substantive  NCC may request further information under section 40. If it is not provided within the specified or extended period, the application is deemed withdrawn, without preventing a fresh application. The rule protects decision quality and prevents incomplete applications remaining indefinitely active.  29.3 A practical assessment framework  Assessment area   Questions  Legal eligibility   Is the applicant duly constituted and eligible for the licence category?  Technical competence   Is the proposed architecture feasible, safe, interoperable and standards-compliant?  Financial capacity   Can the applicant fund deployment and continuing obligations?  Ownership and governance   Who controls the applicant, and are disclosures complete?  Competition   Would grant strengthen entry or create concentration, foreclosure or cross-ownership concerns?  Resources   Are required spectrum, numbers, codes or rights available?  Public interest   Does the proposal advance access, quality, resilience, security and consumer welfare?  29.4 Undertakings  Section 42 allows certain individual grants to be conditional on registration of undertakings and permits specified benefits to be limited to licensees with current registered undertakings. An undertaking is a formal commitment, not a casual promise in a business plan.  EXAM TRAP - Submission is not approval; payment of a processing fee is not grant; technical viability is not complete legal eligibility; and a licence application does not reserve scarce resources unless the framework says so.

NCC Promotion Exam - Controlled Teaching Expansion v4.0 - Checkpoint 3   Page 174  DEEP CHAPTER 30 - THE 90-DAY STATUTORY RULE  30.1 What section 41 actually says  For an individual-licence application that is not subject to a competitive bid process, NCC must within 90 days of receiving it notify the applicant whether the licence is granted, identify special or additional conditions if granted, or give reasons if refused.  If NCC neither grants nor refuses within 90 days, the application is deemed refused at the end of that period unless the applicant later receives written approval. Silence is therefore not statutory approval.  30.2 Do not apply the rule mechanically  •   The rule concerns individual licences outside a competitive-bid process.  •   The statutory period begins from receipt of the application, but completeness and additional-information events must be read with section 40 and applicable procedures.  •   A competitive auction or tender follows its published timetable and rules.  •   A deemed refusal does not prevent later written approval under the wording of section 41(2).  •   Current service-delivery targets may be shorter than the statutory maximum; confirm the current published target before quoting it.  30.3 Refusal needs reasons  Written reasons support transparency, permit the applicant to understand deficiencies, improve administrative accountability and create a record for review or a fresh application. Reasons should connect to published eligibility, evidence, resource limits or statutory objectives rather than vague preference.  30.4 Approval may contain conditions  A grant is not necessarily unconditional. The approval may identify special or additional conditions, and the licensee must also comply with the Act, subsidiary legislation and applicable general conditions.  EXAM TRAP - The Act does not say an application is automatically approved after 90 days. It says the opposite: it is deemed refused unless later written approval is received.

NCC Promotion Exam - Controlled Teaching Expansion v4.0 - Checkpoint 3   Page 175  DEEP CHAPTER 31 - RESOURCE-DEPENDENT LICENSING  31.1 The second gate  Some applications can satisfy corporate and technical eligibility yet still depend on a scarce or coordinated resource. Spectrum, numbering, signalling codes, short codes, orbital coordination, rights of way or interconnection arrangements may affect whether and when the service can operate.  Authorisation   What it permits   Separate dependency  Service licence   Provision of the defined communications service.   May require spectrum, numbers or facilities.  Spectrum assignment/licence   Use of defined frequencies under technical conditions.   Does not by itself authorise every retail service.  Number allocation   Use of numbering resources according to the Numbering Plan.  Depends on eligibility and utilisation controls.  Type approval   Conformity of relevant equipment with technical requirements.  Does not authorise the provider's business activity.  Right-of-way approval   Access to land corridors under applicable law/process.  Does not replace communications licensing.  31.2 One project, multiple approvals  A mobile network project may require an individual service licence, spectrum rights, numbering, type-approved equipment, environmental and planning approvals, site access and interconnection. These permissions have different decision-makers and legal effects. Project management must map dependencies rather than treating 'NCC licence' as one universal approval.  31.3 Your internal Information Technology perspective  A licensing system such as the Licensing and Authorisation Management System should record service category, applicant identity, workflow stage, assessments, conditions, resource dependencies, approval evidence, payments, issuance, renewal and audit history. Digitising a weak process does not cure unclear authority or missing evidence; system controls should reflect the statutory workflow.  LEVEL 10 INSIGHT - Ask two questions: is the applicant qualified, and are all required regulated resources and related approvals available? Passing the first gate does not guarantee the second.

NCC Promotion Exam - Controlled Teaching Expansion v4.0 - Checkpoint 3   Page 176  DEEP CHAPTER 32 - RENEWAL OF AN INDIVIDUAL LICENCE  32.1 Renewal is continued authority, not automatic extension  Under section 43, the licensee may apply not later than six months before expiry. The renewal fee becomes payable upon approval. The wording makes timely application part of regulatory continuity.  32.2 If NCC does not intend to renew  •   NCC must inform the licensee in writing not later than three months from receipt of the renewal application of its refusal to renew.  •   It must notify and publish its intention at least 30 days before expiry in at least one national daily newspaper.  •   Refusal may be based on failure to comply with the licence, the Act or subsidiary legislation, or an instrument issued by NCC.  •   The affected licensee must receive a reasonable opportunity of not less than 14 days to submit written representations.  •   NCC must consider the submission.  32.3 Pending renewal  Section 47(3) protects continuity where the licence has expired but the licensee proves that a renewal application was made in accordance with section 43 and remains pending. It may continue as if the licence had not expired. This is not a general grace period for late applicants.  32.4 Renewal assessment  NCC should review compliance history, fees, rollout and service performance, resource utilisation, ownership, consumer issues, public interest and any updated framework. Renewal is a control point for accountability, but conditions and decisions must remain lawful and procedurally fair.  EXAM TRAP - Six months is the latest statutory point for applying under section 43, not the automatic duration of a renewed licence. Thirty days concerns publication before expiry; fourteen days concerns the minimum representation period.

NCC Promotion Exam - Controlled Teaching Expansion v4.0 - Checkpoint 3   Page 177  DEEP CHAPTER 33 - SURRENDER, SUSPENSION AND REVOCATION  33.1 Three different exits  Action   Who initiates   Effect  Surrender   Licensee gives written notice under section 44.   Voluntary and generally irrevocable once effective, subject to the limited later-date withdrawal mechanism.  Suspension   NCC temporarily removes authority under section 45 and specifies duration and consequences under section 46.  Operations are restricted for the defined period; spectrum consequences may apply.  Revocation   NCC terminates the licence under section 45.   Licensee loses the right to provide the licensed service, subject to transition authorisation.  33.2 Grounds under section 45  Grounds include unpaid amounts or fines; breach of the Act, subsidiary legislation or licence; contravention of other communications-relevant written law; failure to comply with an NCC instrument; insolvency, receivership, liquidation, winding-up or dissolution circumstances; and public interest.  33.3 Rectification and due process  For grounds under paragraphs (a)-(d), suspension or revocation occurs only after written breach notice and a demand to rectify a capable breach within 60 days, followed by failure to rectify. NCC must then give written notice of intention and reasons. The licensee receives at least 14 days for written submissions, which NCC must consider. Subject to those steps, suspension or revocation takes effect 30 days after service of the declaration notice.  33.4 Publication  After the action takes effect, NCC must publish it in at least one national daily newspaper as soon as practicable. Delay or failure to publish does not invalidate the action.  EXAM TRAP - Suspension and revocation are not casual immediate reactions to every breach. The Act contains notice, rectification and representation safeguards for specified grounds.

NCC Promotion Exam - Controlled Teaching Expansion v4.0 - Checkpoint 3   Page 178  DEEP CHAPTER 34 - CONSUMER CONTINUITY AFTER EXIT  34.1 Loss of authority  When revocation, surrender or expiry takes effect, the licensee immediately loses the right to provide the licensed service. Continuing service can itself attract the section 31(2) consequence unless a statutory exception or written transitional authorisation applies.  34.2 Section 47 transition power  NCC may authorise temporary continued operation to wind up affairs, relocate consumers to another licensee, arrange continued service or conduct necessary ancillary activities. This prevents regulatory action from producing avoidable consumer chaos.  34.3 A transition plan should address  •   Customer notification in plain language and sufficient time.  •   Porting, migration or transfer options and preservation of numbers where applicable.  •   Treatment of prepaid balances, deposits, billing disputes and refunds.  •   Continuity of emergency, enterprise and critical services.  •   Records, lawful data retention, privacy and access by successor arrangements.  •   Interconnection, spectrum, numbering and infrastructure dependencies.  •   Final reporting, asset decommissioning and verification of cessation.  34.4 The public-interest balance  Consumer continuity does not erase the breach or revive the licence. It is a controlled bridge from an exiting licensee to a lawful outcome. NCC must avoid allowing transition authority to become indefinite unlicensed operation.  LEVEL 10 INSIGHT - Effective enforcement protects both regulatory credibility and consumers. A strong answer imposes consequences while planning continuity, remediation and verified exit.

NCC Promotion Exam - Controlled Teaching Expansion v4.0 - Checkpoint 3   Page 179  DEEP CHAPTER 35 - CLASS-LICENCE REGISTRATION AND DE-REGISTRATION  35.1 Sections 49-52  NCC may grant a class licence with standard terms and conditions. A person intending to operate under it must submit the prescribed registration notice and pay the prescribed registration fee as a condition precedent. Except where the Act provides otherwise, operation cannot begin until NCC registers the person.  35.2 Why registration still matters  The class licence supplies common legal conditions; registration links a particular operator to those conditions, gives NCC an accountable identity and creates a record for monitoring. It is general authorisation plus individual registration, not permissionless activity.  35.3 De-registration  NCC may de-register for unpaid amounts, failure to comply with the Act, subsidiary legislation or licence conditions, breach of communications-relevant written law, failure to comply with an NCC instrument, or public interest. Cancellation immediately removes the right to provide the class-licensed service.  The statutory text of section 51(2) uses wording that appears internally awkward by saying 'until such time as the Commission may decide to de-register the person' after cancellation. For examination purposes, do not invent a correction; state the clear effect that cancellation removes the right, and consult the official Act for exact wording.  35.4 Registers  NCC must maintain registers of class licences, registered persons, declarations affecting standard conditions and cancellation notices. The register supports transparency, verification and institutional memory.  EXAM TRAP - An operator under a class licence is still a licensee subject to conditions. Individual grant and class registration differ in method, not in the need for compliance.

Before issuing a direction, it gives written notice describing the required compliance and an opportunity to be heard or make a written submission.  After considering the reasons, NCC may direct specified corrective action. Written notice of the direction must be given not later than 30 days from the decision, and the person must comply. NCC may modify, vary or revoke directions using the same procedural approach. Failure to comply can attract a fine, and directions must be registered.  36.2 The compliance ladder  Stage   Purpose   Possible output  Monitoring   Detect whether obligations are being met.   Reports, inspections, measurements and complaint patterns.  Inquiry / information request   Understand facts and obtain records.   Verified evidence and licensee explanation.  Notice and engagement   Identify alleged breach and hear the affected person.   Representation, voluntary correction or disputed facts.  Direction / remediation   Require specified action.   Corrective plan, deadline and measurable result.  Administrative or statutory enforcement  Respond to continuing or serious breach.   Fine, suspension, revocation, prosecution or other lawful consequence.  Verification   Confirm compliance and consumer outcome.   Closure, continued supervision or escalation.  36.3 Monitoring is not enforcement  Collecting information does not itself impose punishment. A notice of concern is not a final finding. A direction is not automatically revocation. The legal stage and procedural rights should be stated accurately.  LEVEL 10 INSIGHT - The best regulatory answer shows escalation: evidence, notice, hearing, direction, consequence and verification, while recognising urgent powers where another instrument lawfully provides them.

NCC Promotion Exam - Controlled Teaching Expansion v4.0 - Checkpoint 3   Page 181  DEEP CHAPTER 37 - INTERNAL LICENSING WORKFLOW AND GOVERNANCE  37.1 From e-service submission to defensible decision  •   Intake validates applicant identity, licence category, mandatory information and payment status.  •   Licensing specialists assess eligibility, scope and applicable procedures.  •   Technical units assess network design, resources, standards and interoperability.  •   Economic-analysis and competition functions review market effects where relevant.  •   Spectrum, numbering, legal, finance, consumer, cybersecurity or other units contribute within mandate.  •   Decision authority reviews evidence, recommendations, conditions and approvals.  •   The system issues or records the licence, conditions, validity, obligations and resources.  •   Obligations management monitors reporting, payments, rollout, quality and renewal.  37.2 Separation of duties  The same person should not invisibly submit, assess, approve, issue and alter a licence record. Role-based access, maker-checker controls, approval matrices, audit logs, version history and document integrity reduce error and manipulation.  37.3 Licensing and Authorisation Management System connection  A strong Licensing and Authorisation Management System should preserve the application as submitted, all requests for additional information, assessment comments, approvals, conditions, generated licence, electronic signature status, dispatch evidence, renewal history and every change. Missed-tenure renewals, multi-invoice generation and progress visibility are not merely software features; they affect regulatory continuity and auditability.  37.4 Data quality  An incorrect legal name, service category, validity date or condition can create regulatory and operational risk. EXAM TRAP - Automation does not change statutory authority. A workflow action is valid only when performed by the authorised decision-maker with the required evidence and approvals.

NCC Promotion Exam - Controlled Teaching Expansion v4.0 - Checkpoint 3   Page 182  LEVEL 10 LICENSING APPLICATION DRILLS  Scenario 1 - The application was ignored for 90 days  An applicant claims that silence automatically granted its individual licence. Advise NCC.  MODEL REASONING  Section 41 applies to a non-competitive individual application and requires written notification within 90 days. If NCC neither grants nor refuses within the period, the application is deemed refused, not approved, unless later written approval is received. NCC should verify receipt and completeness, additional-information correspondence and the applicable procedure; communicate the correct status and reasons; address the administrative failure; and preserve the applicant's ability to pursue the appropriate review or fresh process.  Scenario 2 - Licence transfer through a private agreement  Company A announces that Company B will operate under A's licence after buying its business. Under section 38 the grant is personal and cannot be operated, assigned, sub-licensed or transferred without NCC's prior written approval. NCC should examine the transaction's substance, buyer eligibility, competition, resources, liabilities, consumer continuity and licence conditions before approving, conditioning or refusing it.  Scenario 3 - Repeated breach before revocation  NCC should identify the statutory ground, give written breach notice and a 60-day rectification demand where section 45(2) applies, assess whether the breach is capable of rectification, issue notice of intention and reasons, allow at least 14 days for submissions, consider the response, make the determination and observe the effective-date and publication rules. It should plan customer continuity under section 47.  Scenario 4 - Class licensee starts before registration  The existence of a class licence does not alone authorise an unregistered person. Registration and the prescribed fee are conditions precedent under section 50, subject to statutory exceptions. NCC should confirm the activity and category, stop unlawful operation through the appropriate process, require registration where eligible and address consumer effects.  Scenario 5 - Technically sound but no numbers available  Technical competence does not create numbering resources. Section 33(3) expressly links licensing decisions to available numbers. NCC should verify the Numbering Plan, eligibility and utilisation, consider alternatives, and avoid granting a service scope that cannot lawfully or operationally be supported.

NCC Promotion Exam - Controlled Teaching Expansion v4.0 - Checkpoint 3   Page 183  LICENSING EXAM TRAPS AND RAPID RECALL  Trap   Correct position  A licence is proof of fee payment.   It is legal authority with scope, conditions, term and continuing obligations.  Licence-exempt means illegal.   It means lawfully exempted; unlicensed operation without authority is illegal.  Class licence needs no NCC action.   The person must register and pay the prescribed fee, subject to exceptions.  NCC must use auctions for all licences.   Section 33 permits several published procedures; method depends on the activity and objectives.  Equal treatment means identical conditions.   Relevant differences may justify different conditions under transparent, fair criteria.  An application is approved after 90 days.   For the specified non-competitive individual process, silence produces deemed refusal.  The licence may be sold with the company assets.  Prior written NCC approval is required for operation, assignment, sub-licensing or transfer.  Renewal is automatic if fees are paid.   Timely application and compliance assessment remain necessary.  Revocation ends all service immediately in every case.  Authority ends, but NCC may authorise a controlled transition for consumers and winding up.  A direction is the same as revocation.   A direction requires corrective action; suspension or revocation is a separate consequence.  THE 25-SECOND LICENSING ANSWER  The Nigerian Communications Act requires a licence or lawful exemption to operate communications systems or facilities or provide services. NCC classifies activities as individual, class-licensed or exempt; publishes procedures; assesses eligibility and scarce-resource availability; grants authority with conditions; monitors compliance; controls transfer and renewal; and may direct remediation, de-register, suspend or revoke through applicable due process while protecting consumers.  SELF-CHECK  •   Can I distinguish licence, condition, exemption and registration?  •   Can I explain sections 31-33 without confusing requirement, class and procedure?  •   Can I state the 90-day rule correctly?  •   Can I distinguish renewal, surrender, suspension, revocation and de-registration?  •   Can I explain why service, spectrum, numbering and type approval are separate?  •   Can I design a defensible digital licensing workflow with audit controls?
