NCC Promotion Exam - Controlled Teaching Expansion v4.0 - Checkpoint 4   Page 186  DEEP CHAPTER 38 - WHY NETWORKS MUST CONNECT  38.1 A network is valuable because it reaches beyond itself  A subscriber on Network A expects to call, message or exchange data with a subscriber or service on Network B. Interconnection is the physical and logical linking of communications systems so traffic can pass between separately operated networks. Without it, each network becomes an island.  USER A   NETWORK A   POINT OF INTERCONNECTION   NETWORK B   USER B  Interconnection lets traffic cross network boundaries; each operator still controls its own network domain.  Physical linking includes transmission facilities, ports, equipment and points where networks meet. Logical linking includes signalling, addressing, routing, service control and traffic-management arrangements that allow the networks to understand and deliver the traffic.  38.2 The network effect  The usefulness of a communications network generally increases as the number of reachable users and services grows. A large incumbent could exploit this effect by refusing or degrading interconnection with a smaller entrant. Interconnection regulation therefore supports both end-to-end communication and fair competition.  38.3 Consumer choice depends on interoperability  If customers could communicate only within their own operator, changing provider would become costly and competition would weaken. Reliable interconnection lets users choose networks while remaining connected to the wider communications community.  EXAM TRAP - Interconnection is not simply two companies signing a commercial contract. It is technical connectivity plus regulated commercial, quality, information and continuity obligations.

NCC Promotion Exam - Controlled Teaching Expansion v4.0 - Checkpoint 4   Page 187  DEEP CHAPTER 39 - THE TECHNICAL JOURNEY  39.1 From calling party to called party  •   The originating network authenticates and serves its subscriber.  •   Number analysis and routing determine that the destination belongs to another network.  •   Signalling requests establishment of the cross-network communication.  •   Traffic moves through a defined Point of Interconnection and associated transmission capacity.  •   The terminating network locates or routes toward its subscriber and completes the service where possible.  •   Usage records support charging, reconciliation, fraud control, quality analysis and dispute evidence.  39.2 Point of Interconnection  A Point of Interconnection is the defined physical or logical point where traffic is exchanged. It may involve ports, links, signalling and routing arrangements. The point also helps divide operational responsibility: each party must deliver traffic to and accept traffic from the agreed interface according to the agreement and regulatory framework.  Element   Function   Failure symptom  Transmission link   Carries inter-network traffic.   Total or partial cross-network failure.  Signalling   Coordinates call/session establishment and control.   Call setup failure despite available bearer capacity.  Routing tables   Direct traffic to the appropriate network and point.   Misrouting, loops or unreachable numbers.  Interconnect capacity   Provides enough channels or bandwidth for demand.   Busy-hour congestion and failed attempts.  Clocking/synchronisation   Supports stable operation in relevant legacy and transport environments.  Errors, slips or degraded service.  Charging records   Measure inter-operator traffic for settlement.   Billing disputes and revenue leakage.  39.3 Modern interconnection  Traditional voice interconnection often used circuit-oriented interfaces and signalling. Internet Protocol interconnection carries packet-based services and can support voice, messaging and data. Technology changes, but the regulatory questions remain: feasibility, quality, capacity, security, interoperability, fair terms and continuity.  LEVEL 10 INSIGHT - A Point of Interconnection is both an engineering boundary and an accountability boundary. Good agreements define what each party must deliver, measure and repair on each side.

NCC Promotion Exam - Controlled Teaching Expansion v4.0 - Checkpoint 4   Page 188  DEEP CHAPTER 40 - SECTION 96: THE DUTY TO INTERCONNECT  40.1 The statutory trigger  Section 96 applies when a network services or facilities provider receives an interconnection request from another licensee. The requested provider must interconnect its communications system at technically feasible locations, following section 97 principles and terms negotiated in good faith.  40.2 Four elements  Element   Meaning  Request from another licensee   The obligation is triggered by a recognised interconnection request, not a vague commercial approach.  Network service or facilities provider   The requested party must control relevant network capabilities.  Technically feasible location   The duty is real but not detached from engineering possibility; feasibility must be evidenced, not merely asserted.  Good-faith negotiation   Parties must genuinely work toward lawful terms rather than delay, conceal information or impose impossible demands.  40.3 Technical feasibility  Feasibility can depend on network topology, interface standards, capacity, location, security, resilience, power, transmission and implementation time. A provider claiming infeasibility should identify the specific constraint, evidence it and consider reasonable alternatives. Commercial inconvenience is not automatically technical impossibility.  40.4 Good faith  Good faith is shown by timely responses, competent negotiating teams, disclosure of necessary technical information, realistic proposals, documented reasons and willingness to resolve issues. Repeated postponement, contradictory demands, refusal to identify a feasible point or using confidential information to harm a rival can indicate failure.  EXAM TRAP - Section 96 does not create an unconditional right to connect at any location chosen by the requester. It requires technically feasible locations and good-faith negotiation under the statutory principles.

NCC Promotion Exam - Controlled Teaching Expansion v4.0 - Checkpoint 4   Page 189  DEEP CHAPTER 41 - SECTION 97: AGREEMENT AND NCC INTERVENTION  41.1 Agreements must be written  All interconnection agreements between licensees must be in writing and comply with the Act, NCC regulations and guidelines. They must also comply with neutrality, transparency, non-discrimination, fair competition, universal coverage, access to information, equality of access and equal terms and conditions.  41.2 Party negotiation comes first  The parties primarily agree the terms and conditions. This recognises commercial and technical expertise and allows arrangements to fit their networks. It does not remove NCC oversight or permit contracting out of statutory duties.  41.3 When NCC may intervene and make binding rulings  •   The agreement or a provision is inconsistent with the Act or subsidiary legislation.  •   The parties fail to reach consensus on specific issues.  •   There is delay in reaching consensus.  •   NCC considers intervention to be in the public interest, even without invitation from either party.  41.4 Why the principles matter  Principle   Interconnection meaning  Neutrality   Terms should not improperly favour an affiliate, technology or commercial strategy.  Transparency   Material procedures and terms should be knowable and reviewable.  Non-discrimination / equality   Comparable parties should receive comparable access and quality on relevant terms.  Fair competition   An operator should not use control of connectivity to foreclose rivals.  Universal coverage   Interconnection should support broad reach rather than fragmented islands.  Access to information   Parties need sufficient technical and operational information to connect safely.  LEVEL 10 INSIGHT - NCC intervention is not a failure of market negotiation; it is the statutory safeguard when private bargaining cannot protect legality, competition or the public interest.

NCC Promotion Exam - Controlled Teaching Expansion v4.0 - Checkpoint 4   Page 190  DEEP CHAPTER 42 - REGISTRATION AND REGULATORY REVIEW  42.1 The 30-day registration rule  Section 98 requires either or both parties to register an executed interconnection agreement with NCC within 30 days of execution. Registration creates an official record and brings the agreement within regulatory review.  42.2 NCC may request additional information  The Commission may require further information about the agreement. This can include traffic forecasts, technical diagrams, capacity, quality, rates, costing, security, implementation milestones or evidence that comparable operators receive fair treatment.  42.3 Revision power  After evaluating terms, conditions and charges, NCC may require revision where the agreement is inconsistent with the Act, regulations, interconnection guidelines or public-network integrity. Registration is therefore not a passive filing cabinet exercise.  42.4 What a review should test  Review area   Questions  Authority and form   Are both parties properly licensed and is the agreement executed?  Technical integrity   Are interfaces, routing, capacity, security and resilience workable?  Quality   Are service levels measurable and aligned with applicable rules?  Charges   Are methodologies and settlement terms lawful and non-discriminatory?  Competition   Do terms foreclose entry, favour affiliates or exploit dependency?  Continuity   Are fault, congestion, emergency and disconnection procedures controlled?  Information   Are confidentiality rules balanced with operational and regulatory needs?  EXAM TRAP - Registration does not necessarily mean NCC negotiated every clause. The parties primarily agree terms, while NCC registers, evaluates and may require revision or intervene.

NCC Promotion Exam - Controlled Teaching Expansion v4.0 - Checkpoint 4   Page 191  DEEP CHAPTER 43 - SECTION 99: WHAT REGULATIONS MUST ADDRESS  43.1 Model terms and regulatory structure  Section 99 requires NCC to make interconnection regulations and permits model terms and conditions. The Act identifies seven subject areas that the regulatory framework must address.  Statutory area   Why it matters  Negotiation time and procedures   Prevents delay from becoming a market-entry weapon.  Quality and levels of service   Defines measurable delivery, congestion, availability and repair expectations.  Rate methodologies   Controls how charges are derived and reviewed.  Intellectual property   Protects legitimate rights without obstructing necessary interconnection.  Commercial information   Protects sensitive data while permitting operations and oversight.  Provisioning of facilities   Defines links, ports, capacity, testing, activation and expansion.  Sharing technical information   Enables planning, routing, fault handling and safe interoperability.  43.2 Reference Interconnection Offer  A Reference Interconnection Offer is a published standard offer, usually required from an operator with specified market or regulatory obligations, setting out baseline technical and commercial terms. It reduces repeated negotiation, increases transparency and makes discrimination easier to detect. It remains subject to NCC approval or review under the applicable framework.  43.3 Agreement hierarchy  The Act and operative regulations prevail over inconsistent private terms. The approved reference offer can establish a baseline. The bilateral agreement then records agreed implementation details. Operational schedules translate obligations into contacts, routing, capacity, testing, billing and fault processes.  EXAM TRAP - A Reference Interconnection Offer is not the same as the signed bilateral agreement. It is the regulated baseline offer from which compliant agreements may be concluded.

NCC Promotion Exam - Controlled Teaching Expansion v4.0 - Checkpoint 4   Page 192  DEEP CHAPTER 44 - CHARGES, TERMINATION AND SETTLEMENT  44.1 Why money changes hands  When traffic originating on one network terminates on another, the terminating network uses switching, transport, radio or fixed-access resources to complete the service. Interconnection charges compensate defined network functions according to the applicable methodology and agreement.  44.2 Termination rate  A termination rate is the regulated or agreed charge for completing traffic on another network. It is not the retail price paid by the caller. The retail tariff may include origination, transit, termination, commercial costs, taxes and pricing strategy.  Concept   Meaning   Do not confuse with  Origination   Network function that starts traffic from the calling user.   Termination on the destination network.  Transit   A third network carries traffic between networks.   Direct bilateral interconnection.  Termination   Destination network completes traffic to its user.   Retail call price.  Settlement   Operators reconcile measured traffic and amounts owed.   Consumer billing.  Bill-and-keep   Each party generally retains revenue from its own customers rather than paying per-unit termination, under the applicable arrangement.  Free service or absence of costs.  44.3 Cost orientation and asymmetry  A rate methodology may examine efficient network costs, traffic direction, technology, scale and policy objectives. Asymmetric rates may temporarily reflect material cost differences or entry policy, but can distort incentives if unsupported or prolonged. Symmetry is not automatically fair in every transitional market, and asymmetry is not automatically pro-competitive.  44.4 Traffic measurement disputes  Parties should agree measurement points, time synchronisation, rounding, call records, excluded traffic, dispute windows, audit and reconciliation. A small technical definition can materially change invoices.  LEVEL 10 INSIGHT - Analyse wholesale and retail prices separately. A lower termination rate may reduce wholesale cost, but consumer benefit depends on competition and retail pass-through.

NCC Promotion Exam - Controlled Teaching Expansion v4.0 - Checkpoint 4   Page 193  DEEP CHAPTER 45 - QUALITY, CAPACITY AND CONGESTION  45.1 Interconnection quality is end-to-end quality  A subscriber may have good access-network conditions yet experience failed cross-network calls because the Point of Interconnection is congested, signalling is misconfigured or the other network is unavailable. Interconnection quality must therefore be analysed separately from on-net quality.  45.2 Capacity planning  •   Exchange traffic forecasts and growth assumptions.  •   Define initial links, ports or bandwidth and redundancy.  •   Set utilisation thresholds that trigger augmentation.  •   Provide lead times for ordering, provisioning, testing and activation.  •   Measure busy-hour traffic and failed attempts.  •   Plan overflow, rerouting and disaster recovery.  45.3 Quality indicators  Indicator   What it can reveal  Interconnect availability   Whether the cross-network interface was operational.  Congestion / blocking   Whether demand exceeded provisioned capacity.  Call or session setup success   Whether signalling and routing completed requests.  Post-dial delay / setup time   Whether cross-network establishment is timely.  Answer-seizure or completion ratios   Traffic outcome patterns requiring careful interpretation.  Fault restoration time   Operational responsiveness after failure.  45.4 Historical benchmarks  The baseline preserves older figures for link availability, bit-error rate, Grade of Service, Mean Time to Repair and channel loading. They remain historical or instrument-specific until verified against the operative instrument and methodology. A number without service definition, measurement point and time window is not a safe current answer.  EXAM TRAP - A national Quality of Service average cannot prove that an individual Point of Interconnection is healthy. Interconnect evidence must be traffic-, route-, network- and time-specific.

NCC Promotion Exam - Controlled Teaching Expansion v4.0 - Checkpoint 4   Page 194  DEEP CHAPTER 46 - DISCONNECTION AND SERVICE CONTINUITY  46.1 Section 100 is deliberately strict  Regardless of private agreement terms, a party must not disconnect or discontinue interconnection at any time or in any circumstance without NCC's prior written approval. The rule protects consumers and the integrity of the national communications system from unilateral commercial action.  46.2 Why unilateral disconnection is dangerous  •   Subscribers lose reachability through no fault of their own.  •   Emergency and critical communications may fail.  •   Businesses, banks and public services can be disrupted.  •   A dominant network can use disconnection to discipline or exclude a rival.  •   Traffic may reroute unpredictably or overload other links.  •   The factual and financial dispute becomes harder to resolve after service collapse.  46.3 Approval assessment  Question   Regulatory concern  What is the breach or debt?   Is it established, material and linked to the agreement?  What traffic and users will be affected?   Consumer, emergency, enterprise and systemic consequences.  Can a lesser measure work?   Security, escrow, payment plan, partial restriction or supervised remediation.  What notice is needed?   Fairness and time for users and networks to prepare.  How will traffic be restored?   Clear conditions, contacts and verification.  Is competition affected?   Prevent strategic foreclosure disguised as debt recovery.  46.4 Technical isolation versus regulatory disconnection  An urgent technical action may be necessary to contain a cyberattack, signalling storm or threat to network integrity. The operator should follow applicable emergency procedures, minimise scope, document reasons, notify NCC and restore service. It should not re-label a commercial disconnection as emergency engineering.  EXAM TRAP - A contractual right to terminate does not override section 100's requirement for prior written NCC approval to disconnect interconnection.

NCC Promotion Exam - Controlled Teaching Expansion v4.0 - Checkpoint 4   Page 195  DEEP CHAPTER 47 - ACCESS UNDER SECTIONS 101-103  47.1 Access is broader than traffic exchange  Subject to published exemptions, a network facilities or services provider must provide reasonable access to facilities or services on the access list when requested in writing by another network-facilities provider, network-services provider, applications-service provider or content-applications-service provider.  47.2 The equivalence requirement  The technical standard and quality supplied to the requesting provider must be at least the same as, or more favourable than, what the first provider supplies on its own network facilities or services. This guards against self-preferencing and degraded wholesale access.  47.3 The access list  NCC determines and registers facilities, network services and other facilities or services that facilitate network or applications services. The statutory obligation is therefore structured through an access list, not an assumption that every asset must always be shared.  47.4 Sections 97-100 extend to access  Section 103 applies the agreement, registration, regulation and discontinuance safeguards to access, with necessary adjustments. Written terms, NCC oversight and continuity therefore matter beyond classical interconnection.  Interconnection   Access  Links networks so traffic can pass between them.   Allows another provider to use specified facilities or services.  Focus: end-to-end reachability and traffic exchange.   Focus: an input needed to provide downstream services.  Example: voice traffic exchanged at a Point of Interconnection.   Example: access to listed ducts, facilities or wholesale network service.  LEVEL 10 INSIGHT - Interconnection is a form of network relationship; access is the wider regulated availability of specified inputs. Do not use the words as perfect synonyms.

NCC Promotion Exam - Controlled Teaching Expansion v4.0 - Checkpoint 4   Page 196  DEEP CHAPTER 48 - COLLOCATION AND INFRASTRUCTURE SHARING  48.1 Collocation  Collocation allows one operator to place equipment at another operator's site, building, shelter, tower or facility under agreed conditions. It can include space, power, cooling, security, cable routes and access procedures.  48.2 Passive and active sharing  Type   Examples   Regulatory issues  Passive sharing   Towers, poles, ducts, trenches, shelters, power, cooling, dark fibre and site space.  Safety, capacity, access, pricing, maintenance and rights of way.  Active sharing   Radio equipment, transmission capacity, antennas, Radio Access Network elements or core functions depending on the model.  Control, quality, security, spectrum, resilience, competition and lawful interception.  48.3 Why sharing is encouraged  Sharing can reduce duplicated construction, lower capital and operating cost, accelerate coverage, reduce environmental impact and make rural deployment more viable. It can also improve use of scarce sites and rights of way.  48.4 Why sharing needs safeguards  A facility owner can delay access, reserve capacity for itself, inflate price, provide inferior quality or misuse a rival's confidential plans. Excessive dependence on one shared facility can create a single point of failure. Deep active sharing can also weaken infrastructure competition or facilitate coordination between rivals.  48.5 Capacity is not a magic refusal  A provider claiming no capacity should show engineering evidence, existing commitments, safety limits and expansion possibilities. The requester should provide accurate equipment, load, space and timing needs. NCC can then distinguish genuine constraint from strategic refusal.  EXAM TRAP - Infrastructure sharing is not interconnection. Sharing concerns use of assets or facilities; interconnection concerns the linking of networks to exchange traffic.

NCC Promotion Exam - Controlled Teaching Expansion v4.0 - Checkpoint 4   Page 197  DEEP CHAPTER 49 - SHARING AGREEMENTS AND OPERATIONS  49.1 What an agreement should control  Area   Operational questions  Scope and capacity   Which assets, locations, space, power and load are included?  Access and security   Who may enter, when, under what identification and supervision?  Installation standards   Who approves designs, performs work and certifies safety?  Maintenance   Who maintains shared and customer equipment, and within what times?  Charges   How are recurring, one-off, power, upgrade and restoration costs calculated?  Service levels   What availability, response, escalation and repair commitments apply?  Expansion   How are additional space, load, ports or fibre requested and allocated?  Exit   How are equipment removal, consumer continuity and outstanding charges handled?  49.2 Power and resilience  Tower and site sharing in Nigeria frequently depends on grid availability, generators, batteries, fuel logistics and security. A shared site can remain physically standing while services fail because the energy system is unavailable. Agreements should allocate responsibility for power quality, fuel, preventive maintenance, alarms and restoration.  49.3 Planned maintenance  The facility provider should give reasonable notice, coordinate windows, limit simultaneous risk and provide emergency contacts. The tenant should disclose sensitive services and maintain accurate contact details. Maintenance records help distinguish planned work from avoidable outage.  49.4 Confidentiality  A shared-facility owner may learn a rival's rollout locations, equipment capacity and launch timing. Confidentiality rules should restrict use of that information while allowing NCC access and necessary operational exchange.  LEVEL 10 INSIGHT - A sharing framework must address the physical asset, commercial access, service continuity and competition consequences at the same time.

NCC Promotion Exam - Controlled Teaching Expansion v4.0 - Checkpoint 4   Page 198  DEEP CHAPTER 50 - NATIONAL ROAMING  50.1 What roaming means  Roaming allows a subscriber of a home network to receive service through a visited network under technical and commercial arrangements. The subscriber retains the home relationship and identity while the visited network supplies radio access and supporting functions.  50.2 National versus international roaming  National roaming   International roaming  Home and visited networks operate within Nigeria.   Subscriber uses a network in another country.  Can support coverage, entry, resilience and domestic infrastructure efficiency.  Supports continuity while travelling and depends on cross-border commercial arrangements.  Governed by Nigerian licensing, competition, spectrum, consumer and roaming rules.  Also involves foreign regulation, currency, international signalling and settlement.  50.3 The 2021 framework  NCC's Guidelines on National Roaming in Nigeria 2021 provide the operative guideline anchor in the controlled source set. Commercial agreements remain subject to NCC oversight and relevant licence conditions. The guidelines should be studied as their own instrument rather than inferred from international roaming practice.  50.4 Technical operation  •   The visited network detects and serves the roaming device where an agreement and coverage exist.  •   The home and visited networks exchange authentication and subscriber/service information.  •   Routing determines how voice, messaging and data traffic reach the home network or service destination.  •   Usage records support wholesale settlement and the subscriber's retail bill.  •   Service restrictions, emergency access, quality and lawful requirements must be controlled.  50.5 Why national roaming is not infrastructure sharing  Roaming supplies service to another operator's subscribers. Infrastructure sharing supplies use of network assets or functions. A roaming agreement can exist without tower sharing, and tower sharing can exist without subscriber roaming.  EXAM TRAP - National roaming does not transfer the subscriber permanently to the visited network and is not the same as Mobile Number Portability.

NCC Promotion Exam - Controlled Teaching Expansion v4.0 - Checkpoint 4   Page 199  DEEP CHAPTER 51 - ROAMING BENEFITS AND RISKS  51.1 Potential benefits  •   Faster geographic reach for a new or smaller operator.  •   Coverage continuity where the home network has gaps.  •   Reduced duplication in low-demand locations.  •   Resilience where reciprocal or emergency arrangements are available.  •   More efficient use of already-deployed radio infrastructure.  51.2 Competition risks  A host network may set excessive wholesale prices, provide inferior quality, delay integration, restrict technologies or use roaming to learn a rival's demand. Conversely, a guest operator may rely indefinitely on roaming and under-invest in its own licensed obligations. NCC must balance entry and efficiency against durable infrastructure competition.  51.3 Consumer issues  Issue   Control question  Price   Is the consumer told clearly when domestic roaming changes charges or allowances?  Quality   Can users distinguish visited-network limitations and obtain complaint resolution?  Coverage claims   Does the home operator accurately describe where service depends on roaming?  Emergency service   Does roaming preserve reliable access and location handling?  Privacy/security   Are subscriber and signalling data protected between networks?  Billing   Are records reconciled and disputed charges corrected promptly?  51.4 Roaming and rollout obligations  A licence may require the operator to deploy its own network. Roaming can complement but not automatically replace that obligation. NCC should read the licence, roaming approval and rollout milestones together.  LEVEL 10 INSIGHT - National roaming can simultaneously promote entry and reduce investment incentives. The regulatory answer should specify limits, quality, pricing, transparency and rollout safeguards.

NCC Promotion Exam - Controlled Teaching Expansion v4.0 - Checkpoint 4   Page 200  DEEP CHAPTER 52 - COMPETITION AND DOMINANCE  52.1 Essential facilities and bottlenecks  An input can become a bottleneck when competitors cannot reasonably duplicate it and need it to compete downstream. Examples may include towers in constrained locations, ducts, landing facilities, interconnection gateways or access to a dominant network. Control of a bottleneck can create the power to refuse, delay, degrade or overprice access.  52.2 Forms of discrimination  Conduct   How it can harm competition  Price discrimination   A rival pays more than an affiliate for comparable input.  Quality discrimination   Rival receives slower provisioning, lower capacity or poorer repair.  Information discrimination   Affiliate receives planning or technical information earlier.  Margin squeeze   Wholesale and retail prices leave an efficient rival insufficient margin.  Strategic delay   Negotiation or testing is prolonged until the entrant misses market timing.  Tying/bundling   Access to an essential input is conditioned on unnecessary services.  52.3 Not every difference is discrimination  Different costs, locations, volumes, technologies, risk or service levels can justify different terms. The issue is whether the distinction is objectively relevant, proportionate and consistently applied. Cost evidence and comparable agreements matter.  52.4 Competition and resilience can pull in different directions  Sharing reduces duplication but can concentrate operational dependence. Mandated access helps entrants but can reduce investment incentives if prices do not compensate efficient cost. NCC must design rules that support entry while preserving incentives to build and maintain robust infrastructure.  EXAM TRAP - A dominant position is not automatically unlawful. The regulatory concern is abuse, substantial lessening of competition or failure to meet applicable access/interconnection duties.

NCC Promotion Exam - Controlled Teaching Expansion v4.0 - Checkpoint 4   Page 201  DEEP CHAPTER 53 - DISPUTE RESOLUTION  53.1 Common disputes  •   Whether a requested location or interface is technically feasible.  •   Delay in negotiation, provisioning, testing or capacity expansion.  •   Termination, transit, collocation or power charges.  •   Quality measurement and responsibility for failure.  •   Traffic records, invoices, fraud and settlement differences.  •   Disconnection threats and unpaid debts.  •   Discrimination between an affiliate and competing licensee.  •   Confidential information and forecast use.  53.2 Evidence package  A defensible submission should include the request and response chronology, licence status, agreement and schedules, network diagrams, traffic forecasts, orders, testing results, utilisation, outage logs, quality metrics, invoices, reconciliation records, meeting minutes, correspondence and proposed remedies.  53.3 NCC analytical sequence  •   Define the precise disputed issue and the relief sought.  •   Confirm jurisdiction, licence relationships and operative instruments.  •   Separate agreed facts from disputed facts.  •   Test technical feasibility, capacity and quality evidence.  •   Assess charges and comparable treatment.  •   Examine competition and consumer consequences.  •   Provide procedural fairness and hear both parties.  •   Issue a reasoned, implementable and measurable ruling or direction.  •   Monitor compliance and close only after verification.  53.4 Interim measures  Where consumer or network harm may occur before final resolution, NCC may consider lawful interim continuity or information measures. An interim measure should preserve service and evidence without prejudging the final merits more than necessary.  LEVEL 10 INSIGHT - A good ruling does not merely declare a winner. It identifies the obligation, facts, reasoning, corrective action, deadline, measurement method and consequence of non-compliance.

NCC Promotion Exam - Controlled Teaching Expansion v4.0 - Checkpoint 4   Page 202  DEEP CHAPTER 54 - INTERNAL NCC AND SYSTEM WORKFLOW  54.1 Cross-functional regulation  An interconnection or sharing matter can require licensing, technical, economic-analysis, legal, consumer, spectrum, numbering, finance, cybersecurity and enforcement input. The responsible lead should coordinate these contributions without allowing the case to become ownerless.  54.2 Digital case record  Record   Why it matters  Parties and licence categories   Confirms eligibility, authority and relationships.  Request and negotiation chronology   Tests good faith and delay.  Agreement versions and signatures   Preserves the binding text and amendments.  Technical schedules   Records points, routes, capacity, interfaces and service levels.  Commercial schedules   Records rates, billing, settlement and securities.  Registration and approvals   Proves statutory and internal decision steps.  Faults, disputes and directions   Links performance to remedies and compliance.  Audit history   Shows who changed data, when and under what authority.  54.3 Data relationships  A robust system should connect each agreement to both licensees, relevant licences, Points of Interconnection, access assets, rates, validity, amendments, disputes and approvals. Storing only an uploaded PDF prevents meaningful monitoring. Structured records enable alerts for registration deadlines, capacity thresholds, expiring terms and unresolved disputes.  54.4 Information protection  Interconnection records contain commercially sensitive traffic, cost, topology and security information. Access should follow role and need, while authorised regulatory teams retain enough visibility for oversight. Audit trails should record viewing, download and amendment of sensitive records.  EXAM TRAP - Confidentiality does not prevent submission of information lawfully required by NCC. It governs protection and permitted use after disclosure.

NCC Promotion Exam - Controlled Teaching Expansion v4.0 - Checkpoint 4   Page 203  LEVEL 10 APPLICATION DRILLS  Scenario 1 - Congestion only on off-net calls  Subscribers report successful on-net calls but repeated evening failures to another operator.  MODEL REASONING  The pattern points toward the interconnection path rather than general radio coverage. NCC should compare originating and terminating network counters, Point-of-Interconnection utilisation, signalling failures, route availability, busy-hour forecasts and augmentation requests. It should test whether either party delayed capacity, compare performance with the operative framework and agreement, direct remediation, protect continuity and verify improvement.  Scenario 2 - Unpaid invoices and threatened disconnection  The creditor may pursue settlement remedies, but section 100 prevents unilateral disconnection without NCC's prior written approval. NCC should verify the debt, reconciliation and dispute clauses; assess consumer and systemic harm; consider security, escrow or payment arrangements; evaluate competition concerns; and issue a reasoned decision with continuity and restoration controls.  Scenario 3 - Tower-space refusal  The owner claims the tower has no remaining capacity. NCC should obtain structural-loading analysis, space and power records, existing reservations, safety evidence and expansion options; compare treatment of affiliates; examine the requester's equipment and timing; and distinguish genuine engineering limits from strategic foreclosure.  Scenario 4 - New entrant relies entirely on roaming  Roaming may accelerate entry, but NCC should compare the arrangement with the entrant's rollout obligations, duration, geographic scope, wholesale price, service quality, consumer disclosure and investment plan. Approval should not silently erase licence commitments.  Scenario 5 - Draft regulation cited as current  A party relies on the Draft Telecommunications Networks Interconnection Regulations 2024 as though already operative. NCC should verify whether a final instrument was made and published. Until then, the 2007 Regulations remain the operative listed instrument and the draft is consultation evidence only.

NCC Promotion Exam - Controlled Teaching Expansion v4.0 - Checkpoint 4   Page 204  EXAM TRAPS AND RAPID RECALL  Trap   Correct position  Interconnection means tower sharing.   Interconnection exchanges traffic; sharing provides use of assets or functions.  A Point of Interconnection is only a building.   It is the defined physical/logical traffic-exchange boundary.  Parties are free to agree any terms.   Agreements must comply with the Act, regulations and statutory principles.  NCC negotiates every clause.   Parties primarily agree terms; NCC may intervene and require revision.  Registration is optional after signing.   Section 98 requires registration within 30 days.  A contractual clause permits immediate disconnection.  Section 100 requires prior written NCC approval.  Access and interconnection are identical.   Access concerns listed wholesale facilities/services; interconnection links networks.  National roaming is Mobile Number Portability.   Roaming temporarily uses a visited network; porting changes provider while retaining a number.  Sharing always improves competition.   It can reduce costs but also enable discrimination, dependence or coordination.  The 2024 draft automatically replaced the 2007 rules.  A draft is not operative until lawfully finalised and published.  THE 30-SECOND ANSWER  Interconnection physically and logically links licensed networks so users can communicate across operator boundaries. Sections 96-100 require technically feasible interconnection, good-faith written agreements, statutory principles, registration within 30 days, NCC review and prior written approval before disconnection. Access extends regulated use of listed facilities or services. Roaming serves another operator's subscribers, while infrastructure sharing provides assets or functions; each requires quality, competition, security and continuity safeguards. NCC Promotion Exam - Controlled Teaching Expansion v4.0 - Checkpoint 5   Page 207  DEEP CHAPTER 55 - WHY NUMBERING IS INFRASTRUCTURE  55.1 A number is not merely a label  A communications number is a structured address. It gives networks enough information to identify a service or destination and route communications toward it. The digits printed on a subscriber's screen are the visible end of a national coordination system involving plans, allocations, operator databases, interconnection, signalling, billing, emergency access and consumer records.  DIALLED NUMBER   NUMBER ANALYSIS   ROUTING LOOKUP   DESTINATION NETWORK   REACHABLE USER  A number is useful only when plans, databases and networks interpret it consistently.  Uniqueness matters because two simultaneously active services cannot safely be presented to the public as the same reachable destination. Structure matters because networks must interpret digits consistently. Stability matters because people, businesses and public services build relationships around numbers.  55.2 Why NCC regulates it  No operator can create a nationally interoperable numbering system alone. If each operator invented incompatible meanings, off-net communication would fail. NCC therefore plans and administers numbering resources in the public interest, coordinates their use, prevents harmful conflict, supports competition and ensures that licensees use assigned resources efficiently and lawfully.  55.3 Scarcity is administrative as well as mathematical  Digits can form many combinations, but usable ranges are constrained by the national plan, recognisable service categories, routing design, technology, legacy assignments, reserved capacity and future growth. A badly fragmented or hoarded plan may exhaust convenient space long before every mathematical combination is used.  EXAM TRAP - Numbering and radio spectrum are both nationally managed resources, but a number is a logical address while spectrum is a physical frequency resource used to carry radio energy.

NCC Promotion Exam - Controlled Teaching Expansion v4.0 - Checkpoint 5   Page 208  DEEP CHAPTER 56 - THE NATIONAL NUMBERING PLAN  56.1 The plan is a grammar for digits  A National Numbering Plan tells the sector how communications addresses are organised. It defines categories, lengths, prefixes or access codes, reserved space and rules for expansion. Its purpose is not merely to publish a list. It gives operators and users a common grammar so a sequence of digits has a predictable regulatory and routing meaning.  56.2 International and national presentation  Nigeria's international country code is +234. A number used domestically may be presented with a national trunk prefix; an international presentation removes that domestic access convention and adds the country code. The exact handling belongs to the applicable plan and network configuration. The plus sign is a user-interface convention indicating the international access method, not itself a routed digit in every underlying system.  Layer   Function   Question to ask  Country code   Identifies the national numbering domain internationally.  Which country plan should interpret the following digits?  National significant number   The meaningful national destination portion after the country code.  Which service, range or destination is addressed?  Prefix or access code   Signals a category, network function or service-selection convention.  How should the network analyse the digits?  Subscriber portion   Distinguishes destinations within the applicable range.  Which individual service should receive the communication?  56.3 Plan changes require migration  Changing lengths or prefixes affects switches, routing tables, billing, directories, customer devices, enterprise private-branch exchanges, advertising and public awareness. A regulator therefore needs a migration plan, parallel-running period where appropriate, testing, communication and a clear cutover. A technically correct change can still fail if consumers and interconnected systems are not prepared.  LEVEL 10 INSIGHT - Numbering policy is part engineering, part economics and part public administration. A plan must remain routable today while preserving orderly growth tomorrow.

NCC Promotion Exam - Controlled Teaching Expansion v4.0 - Checkpoint 5   Page 209  DEEP CHAPTER 57 - NUMBER TYPES AND PURPOSES  57.1 Not every number performs the same job  Resource type   Plain-language purpose   Regulatory concern  Geographic or fixed number   Associates a reachable fixed service with an area or numbering structure.  Location meaning, portability, efficient range use.  Mobile number   Addresses a public mobile service and follows the mobile numbering structure.  Scale, portability, identity lifecycle, routing.  Short code   Uses fewer digits for memorable access to emergency, public-interest or commercial services.  Scarcity, collision, transparency, consumer harm.  Freephone or special-tariff number   Uses a defined charging/service convention.   Who pays, disclosure, bill shock and routing.  Machine or Internet-of-Things resource  Supports connected devices or services where an applicable range is designated.  Scale, lifecycle, roaming, security and future capacity.  Signalling or network code   Identifies networks or functions inside communications systems rather than ordinary public dialling.  Uniqueness, technical coordination and authorised use.  57.2 Short codes deserve special care  A short code is easy to remember precisely because it occupies unusually valuable numbering space. Emergency codes must be reachable, consistently routed and protected from commercial confusion. Commercial codes require clear ownership, price disclosure, consent, content accountability and complaint routes. Similar-looking codes can cause misdialling or deception.  57.3 Numbering does not automatically grant a service right  A licensee may need a number to provide an authorised service, but possession of a number does not enlarge its licence. NCC must first confirm the legal service scope and eligibility, then decide whether numbering resources are necessary. Numbering allocation, licence authorisation, interconnection readiness and service approval are related controls, not substitutes for one another.  EXAM TRAP - A short code is not automatically toll-free, emergency or NCC-owned. Its purpose, charging and holder depend on the applicable allocation and rules.

NCC Promotion Exam - Controlled Teaching Expansion v4.0 - Checkpoint 5   Page 210  DEEP CHAPTER 58 - ALLOCATION, ASSIGNMENT AND USE  58.1 Four stages that answers often collapse  Stage   Meaning   Evidence  Planning   NCC defines the structure and reserves space for services and growth.  Numbering plan, policy and internal records.  Allocation or assignment   NCC grants a licensee controlled rights to a block, code or identifier under stated conditions.  Decision, certificate, register and conditions.  Network activation   The operator configures the resource in its systems and interconnected routing.  Implementation and test records.  End-user use   An individual number or code supports a subscriber or service.   Provisioning, registration and usage records.  58.2 What NCC should test before granting resources  •   The applicant holds the relevant licence and the proposed use is within scope.  •   The requested resource category matches the service architecture.  •   Demand forecasts are credible and existing allocations are sufficiently utilised.  •   The applicant can implement routing, portability, emergency, lawful and consumer obligations.  •   The request does not create avoidable fragmentation or sterilise future plan capacity.  •   Fees, reporting, activation milestones and other conditions are understood.  58.3 Allocation is controlled stewardship  The recipient normally receives a right to use the resource for authorised purposes, not private ownership of the national plan. Conditions can include activation, utilisation reporting, prohibition on unauthorised transfer, accurate records and surrender or withdrawal. A company cannot treat dormant blocks as speculative real estate.  58.4 Withdrawal requires control  Recovery may be justified by expiry, non-use, misuse, licence loss or plan reorganisation, but NCC should verify authority, facts, notice, consumer impact and migration. Abrupt recovery can make lawful users unreachable. The remedy should protect the plan without creating disproportionate disruption.  LEVEL 10 INSIGHT - Ask three separate questions: Was the resource lawfully granted? Is it being used within purpose? Is the use efficient enough to justify continued occupation of scarce plan space?

NCC Promotion Exam - Controlled Teaching Expansion v4.0 - Checkpoint 5   Page 211  DEEP CHAPTER 59 - UTILISATION, FORECASTING AND AUDIT  59.1 Why headline allocation figures mislead  A block allocated to an operator is not the same as a number activated, a subscription active, or a unique human subscriber. One person may hold several subscriptions; machine connections may have no human user; reserved, quarantine and test numbers may be unavailable for new issue. Statistics must define their unit and date.  Measure   What it tells NCC   Possible distortion  Allocated capacity   Plan space granted to the operator.   May include unused or reserved numbers.  Activated numbers   Numbers provisioned for service.   May include inactive or duplicate subscriptions.  Active subscriptions   Connections meeting the applicable activity definition.   Not equal to unique persons.  Traffic-bearing numbers   Resources actually generating service use in a period.   Low-use safety or machine services may be valid.  Quarantined numbers   Disconnected numbers withheld before reassignment.   Temporarily unavailable but not wasted.  59.2 Evidence-led forecasting  A credible forecast links customer growth, product launch, historical take-up, churn, existing free inventory, geographic rollout and technical constraints. NCC should compare successive forecasts with actual use. Persistent overstatement may indicate hoarding; persistent underestimation may produce emergency allocations and fragmented routing.  59.3 Reconciliation  Operator inventories, activation platforms, portability records, subscriber databases, billing systems and NCC registers should reconcile. Differences require root-cause analysis: delayed feeds, duplicate records, failed deactivation, incorrect range mapping or unauthorised use. An audit is not complete when totals merely look plausible.  59.4 Good data governance  •   Common definitions and reporting period.  •   Range-level and status-level detail.  •   Validation rules that reject impossible combinations.  •   Named data owners and certification.  •   Immutable submission and amendment audit trails.  •   Exception queues, deadlines and closure evidence.  EXAM TRAP - A low utilisation ratio may justify scrutiny, but it does not by itself prove abuse; deployment stage, quarantine, service design and legitimate resilience requirements must be examined.

NCC Promotion Exam - Controlled Teaching Expansion v4.0 - Checkpoint 5   Page 212  DEEP CHAPTER 60 - HOW A NUMBER BECOMES A ROUTE  60.1 Number analysis  When a user dials, the serving network analyses the digits: Is the format valid? Is it an emergency or short code? Is it national or international? Which destination or service class applies? The network then selects a route and uses signalling to request delivery. Interconnection carries the communication across operator boundaries.  60.2 Prefix routing and its limitation  Historically a prefix could strongly suggest the operator holding the original range. Mobile Number Portability breaks the assumption that the current serving operator must match the visible prefix. A network therefore needs an authoritative portability lookup or routing method before sending traffic.  60.3 Failure patterns  Symptom   Possible numbering or routing cause   Evidence  One range unreachable from one network  Missing or wrong route for that range.   Route tables, signalling traces, test calls.  Ported numbers fail   Stale portability information or incorrect onward routing.   Port database records, timestamps, donor/recipient logs.  Short code works on some operators only  Incomplete configuration or agreement.   Per-network tests and activation approvals.  Calls reach wrong service   Translation error, overlapping code or stale assignment.   Dialled digits, switch translation and register.  Unexpected charge   Wrong tariff classification or disclosure failure.   Billing records, tariff approval and customer message.  60.4 End-to-end accountability  The visible symptom may originate in the calling network, portability database, transit path, interconnection, destination network or service platform. NCC should avoid blaming the holder of the displayed prefix without tracing the actual serving and routing state.  LEVEL 10 INSIGHT - Numbering turns human intention into machine routing. Regulation succeeds only when the published plan, NCC allocation register, portability data and network configuration agree.

NCC Promotion Exam - Controlled Teaching Expansion v4.0 - Checkpoint 5   Page 213  DEEP CHAPTER 61 - MOBILE NUMBER PORTABILITY  61.1 The consumer problem  A well-known mobile number has economic and social value. Changing it can require notifying family, clients, banks and digital services. Mobile Number Portability allows a subscriber to retain the number while changing the service provider, reducing this switching cost and strengthening choice.  61.2 Roles  Role   Meaning  Subscriber   The legitimate holder requesting the move.  Donor network   The provider from which the number is ported.  Recipient network   The provider receiving and serving the ported number.  Central portability function   Coordinates authoritative porting data and industry consistency under the applicable architecture.  Other networks   Update or query routing so traffic reaches the recipient network.  61.3 Controlled process  •   The subscriber initiates a request through the prescribed channel.  •   Identity, authorisation and eligibility are checked without creating artificial barriers.  •   The request receives a unique record and timestamp.  •   Donor and recipient exchange the prescribed validation messages.  •   On approval, service and routing records change within a coordinated window.  •   The recipient activates service; all networks route the retained number correctly.  •   The subscriber receives clear status information and can complain if the process fails.  61.4 Competition and protection must coexist  Rules should prevent unjustified refusal or delay by a donor, but should also prevent unauthorised porting. Too little verification invites fraud; excessive friction can defeat competition. The correct design uses proportionate authentication, standard rejection reasons, short controlled timelines, traceable records and rapid reversal or remediation where lawful.  EXAM TRAP - Porting changes the serving provider while retaining the number. It is not a SIM replacement, number change, roaming arrangement or transfer of ownership of numbering resources.

NCC Promotion Exam - Controlled Teaching Expansion v4.0 - Checkpoint 5   Page 214  DEEP CHAPTER 62 - PORTING FAILURES AND FRAUD  62.1 Legitimate rejection versus obstruction  A port request may fail because identity or authorisation is not established, data is inconsistent, the number is in an ineligible state or another defined condition applies. The reason should match the operative rules and be evidenced. Vague or repeated rejection can become an anti-competitive tactic.  Risk   Mechanism   Control  Port-out fraud   Impostor ports the victim's number and receives calls or one-time passwords.  Strong identity checks, alerts, audit and rapid dispute response.  Slamming   Provider change occurs without valid informed consent.   Recorded authorisation and independent verification.  Donor delay   Losing operator uses process friction to retain customer.   Standard timelines, reason codes and performance monitoring.  Routing lag   Port completes but other networks still send traffic incorrectly.  Coordinated activation, database propagation and test calls.  Double service or outage   Cutover states are not synchronised.   Transactional workflow, rollback and reconciliation.  62.2 Complaint investigation  NCC should obtain the subscriber request, verification evidence, timestamps, donor and recipient messages, rejection code, database state, activation logs, routing tests, consumer notices and any linked SIM change. This reconstructs the transaction and distinguishes a legitimate control from obstruction or fraud.  62.3 Key performance view  Useful measures include request volumes, successful ports, rejection rate by reason, processing time, post-port outage, complaints, reversals and operator-specific anomalies. A single overall success percentage may conceal one operator's strategic rejection or one failure reason affecting vulnerable consumers.  LEVEL 10 INSIGHT - Mobile Number Portability is a controlled distributed transaction. Identity, donor release, central record, recipient activation and national routing must move toward one consistent state.

NCC Promotion Exam - Controlled Teaching Expansion v4.0 - Checkpoint 5   Page 215  DEEP CHAPTER 63 - FOUR IDENTIFIERS, FOUR JOBS  63.1 Stop calling everything a SIM number  Identifier   What it identifies   What it does not prove  Mobile Subscriber Integrated Services Digital Network Number (MSISDN)  The publicly reachable mobile service number.   The human identity, physical SIM or device on its own.  International Mobile Subscriber Identity (IMSI)  A subscription identity used by mobile networks for authentication and mobility functions.  The device hardware or public dialling number by itself.  Integrated Circuit Card Identifier (ICCID)   The particular SIM card or embedded profile container issued through the supply chain.  The current user or handset.  International Mobile Equipment Identity (IMEI)  The mobile equipment or handset identity.   The subscriber's entitlement to use the service.  63.2 Why separation matters  A subscriber can replace a damaged SIM and retain the same public number: the card identifier changes while the service number remains. A person can move the SIM into another handset: the equipment identity changes while subscriber and service identities may remain. A port can keep the public number while network-serving relationships change. Investigation therefore needs a time-stamped relationship among identifiers, not one field treated as permanent truth.  63.3 Embedded SIM does not abolish identity control  An embedded Subscriber Identity Module can download and manage operator profiles without inserting a removable plastic card. The form factor changes; the regulator still needs secure provisioning, authorised profile lifecycle, subscriber registration, device compatibility, switching and consumer protection.  63.4 Privacy and proportionality  These identifiers can reveal sensitive relationships and activity. Access should be purpose-limited, role-based, logged and retained only as lawfully required. Staff should not export complete datasets when a targeted query will answer the regulatory question.  EXAM TRAP - A phone number identifies a reachable service, not conclusively the natural person holding the handset at a particular moment.

NCC Promotion Exam - Controlled Teaching Expansion v4.0 - Checkpoint 5   Page 216  DEEP CHAPTER 64 - SUBSCRIBER REGISTRATION AND NIN  64.1 The regulatory objective  Subscriber registration connects a communications service to a sufficiently verified person or authorised organisation. National Identification Number integration strengthens the identity anchor by checking subscriber information against the national identity system. The objective is accountable access and trustworthy records, not collection for its own sake.  64.2 Individual transaction  •   The customer presents the required identity information and requests service.  •   The communications service provider obtains and verifies the National Identification Number through the prescribed interface.  •   Biometric or facial checks establish that the present person corresponds to the identity record.  •   Consent and lawful-use notices govern copying or using foundational information for the service record.  •   Registration data and a live image are captured or aligned as required.  •   The mobile number and subscription are linked to the verified record.  •   Activation occurs only when the applicable controls succeed.  •   The provider retains evidence and supplies required regulatory records securely.  64.3 Verification is not the same as data duplication  Verification answers whether a claim matches an authoritative source. Copying creates another stored dataset with its own accuracy, access, security and retention risks. The process should minimise unnecessary duplication while preserving the functional registration record and audit evidence required by law.  64.4 A failed check is a case, not a licence to improvise  Mismatch, unavailable service, poor biometric capture or suspected impersonation should trigger defined exception handling. Agents must not substitute another person's identity, edit authoritative fields informally or bypass activation controls to meet sales targets.  LEVEL 10 INSIGHT - Identity assurance is a chain. A strong national identity database cannot compensate for weak agent authentication, poor capture, insecure transfer or unauthorised post-verification changes.

NCC Promotion Exam - Controlled Teaching Expansion v4.0 - Checkpoint 5   Page 217  DEEP CHAPTER 65 - COMPLEX SUBSCRIBER CATEGORIES  65.1 Corporate subscriptions  A company cannot present a face or fingerprint. The process must prove the organisation's legal existence, the authority of a designated representative and the association of individual users with lines. The controlled rules use responsible corporate roles and secondary-user validation so a large pool of lines is not hidden behind one unaccountable identity.  Control layer   Question  Entity   Does the organisation exist and do its documents match authoritative records?  Authority   Who may request, change, replace or terminate lines for the organisation?  Primary responsible person   Whose verified identity anchors administration of the account?  Secondary users   Which natural person uses each line where the rules require association?  Change management   How are leavers, reassignment, lost devices and new administrators updated?  Audit   Can the provider reconstruct who authorised each lifecycle event?  65.2 Foreigners and visitors  A lawful user may not possess the same Nigerian identity credentials as a citizen or long-term resident. Rules therefore distinguish relevant categories and alternative documents or activation conditions. The principle is equivalent assurance through the prescribed route, not either exclusion or an uncontrolled exemption.  65.3 Minors, dependants and assisted registration  Where special arrangements apply, the record must distinguish the actual service user from the responsible adult or representative. Assistance must not erase consent, accountability or safeguarding. Staff should consult the operative rule rather than assume a general age or proxy rule.  65.4 Machine-to-machine and Internet-of-Things services  A sensor has no personal biography, but the entity deploying and controlling it is accountable. Registration should connect the resource to the licensed service, responsible organisation, device estate, purpose and lifecycle. High-volume machine deployments demand bulk controls without sacrificing traceability.  EXAM TRAP - Corporate registration does not mean placing every line under a director's name and forgetting the users. Entity authority and line-level accountability are separate controls.

NCC Promotion Exam - Controlled Teaching Expansion v4.0 - Checkpoint 5   Page 218  DEEP CHAPTER 66 - THE NUMBER LIFECYCLE  66.1 A number changes state  A number can be reserved, allocated, activated, used, suspended, barred, disconnected, quarantined, recycled and reassigned. Subscriber, operator and third-party systems must understand these changes. A database that stores only 'active' or 'inactive' cannot represent the risk.  State   Meaning   Control concern  Active   Provisioned for a current service.   Correct identity, lawful use and current routing.  Suspended or barred   Use is restricted while the relationship or investigation may continue.  Reason, authority, notice and restoration.  Disconnected   Service relationship has ended.   Stop charging, cease routing and begin controlled lifecycle.  Quarantine   Number is withheld before possible reuse.   Reduce residual calls, messages and stale-account risk.  Recycled or reassigned   Number is issued to a different subscriber.   Remove old linkage and establish new identity.  66.2 Why recycling is necessary  Permanently locking every disconnected number would eventually waste plan capacity. Recycling returns resources to productive use. But time alone cannot cleanse a number: the operator must remove prior identity links, update required systems, retain lawful history separately and create a clean new registration.  66.3 Why quarantine helps but is not magic  A holding period allows traffic and stale associations to decline, yet banks, social platforms and acquaintances may retain a number for years. The safe answer combines quarantine, cross-system status signals, consumer education and stronger authentication by relying organisations.  66.4 Historical truth must remain auditable  Purging the previous identity from the current assignment does not mean destroying every lawful historical record. Systems should separate current ownership or use from time-bounded history so investigations can reconstruct who held the number on a relevant date without presenting the former subscriber as the present one.  LEVEL 10 INSIGHT - The core data model is temporal: which identity, SIM, device, operator and status were linked to this number at this specific time?

NCC Promotion Exam - Controlled Teaching Expansion v4.0 - Checkpoint 5   Page 219  DEEP CHAPTER 67 - SIM SWAP, SPOOFING AND ACCOUNT TAKEOVER  67.1 SIM replacement  A legitimate subscriber may replace a Subscriber Identity Module after loss, theft, damage or format change while retaining the number. In SIM-swap fraud, an attacker persuades or corrupts the provider into moving the victim's service to a SIM controlled by the attacker. Calls and one-time passwords then reach the attacker.  67.2 Caller identity spoofing  Spoofing manipulates displayed caller or sender identity. A familiar number on the screen is therefore not conclusive proof of origin. Controls may involve signalling integrity, traceability, blocking rules, inter-operator coordination and consumer education. It must be distinguished from number reassignment, where the number has genuinely moved to a new user.  Event   What changes   Principal risk  SIM swap   SIM or profile serving the same number.   Attacker captures service and authentication messages.  Port-out fraud   Serving provider changes without valid subscriber authority.  Attacker moves number to another network.  Reassignment   Number is lawfully issued to a new subscriber after lifecycle controls.  Old third-party accounts still trust it.  Spoofing   Presented identity is manipulated without necessarily controlling the number.  Victim trusts a false display.  Fraudulent registration   Identity record is false, stolen or improperly verified.   Anonymous or misattributed service.  67.3 Defence in depth  •   Strong and proportionate identity checks for replacement and porting.  •   Independent notification through an existing trusted channel.  •   Maker-checker approval for high-risk or exception transactions.  •   Agent authentication, location and device controls.  •   Velocity and anomaly detection across repeated requests.  •   Cooling-off or enhanced verification for sensitive downstream transactions.  •   Rapid consumer reporting, containment and restoration.  •   Evidence preservation and sanctions for insider collusion.  EXAM TRAP - National Identification Number linkage reduces false identity risk but cannot alone prevent an insider from bypassing a SIM-replacement process.

NCC Promotion Exam - Controlled Teaching Expansion v4.0 - Checkpoint 5   Page 220  DEEP CHAPTER 68 - TELECOM IDENTITY RISK MANAGEMENT SYSTEM  68.1 The problem crosses sectors  Banks, financial-technology firms and insurers often use a mobile number for contact, authentication or recovery. They may not know that the number has been churned, reassigned, swapped or blacklisted. The Telecom Identity Risk Management System provides a centralised, secure interface through which authorised telecommunications operators publish relevant status and approved service providers verify it.  68.2 Role separation  Actor   Permitted role shown in current documentation   Why it matters  Telecommunications operator   Updates status for numbers it is authorised to manage.   The source network owns the lifecycle event evidence.  Approved service provider   Verifies status for onboarding, authentication or transactions.   A relying organisation receives a risk signal, not update power.  System administrator/regulatory layer   Approves organisations, credentials and governance.   Participation and access are controlled.  68.3 Statuses are signals, not verdicts  Current documentation describes statuses such as churned, swapped, blacklisted, reassigned, normal and null. A swapped result does not prove fraud; a legitimate customer may have replaced a damaged card. A normal result does not prove that the person presenting the number is the lawful subscriber. Each result should feed a proportionate decision with other evidence.  68.4 Correct status statement  The programme has a consultation and stakeholder-development history. Separate official NCC technical documentation now shows an implementation layer with a production base address, authenticated endpoints, operator updates, service-provider verification and webhooks. This supports saying there is current operational technical evidence. It does not prove that every intended institution is onboarded or every proposed rule is final.  LEVEL 10 INSIGHT - The system does not replace subscriber registration. Registration answers who is linked to the service; identity-risk management adds what has happened to the number over time and whether a relying organisation should apply caution.

NCC Promotion Exam - Controlled Teaching Expansion v4.0 - Checkpoint 5   Page 221  DEEP CHAPTER 69 - APPLICATION PROGRAMMING INTERFACE GOVERNANCE  69.1 The update path  •   An operator detects a lifecycle event such as churn, swap, blacklist or reassignment.  •   Its authorised backend sends a status update through the protected application programming interface.  •   The request includes the number, status and applicable event or reassignment date.  •   The platform validates identity, authority, format and permitted values.  •   The central record is updated and becomes available to authorised verification users.  •   Logs preserve who submitted what and when.  69.2 The verification path  •   An approved relying organisation faces onboarding, password-reset or sensitive-transaction risk.  •   Its backend submits the number in the required format using an authenticated request.  •   The platform returns status, verification outcome and relevant timestamps or network data.  •   The organisation applies its own risk rule, seeks stronger evidence, pauses or proceeds.  •   The decision and basis are logged for review.  69.3 Webhooks and continuous assurance  A webhook lets the system notify a registered endpoint when a previously verified number changes status. This converts a one-time check into event-driven risk management. Delivery must still be authenticated, retried safely, deduplicated and monitored; otherwise a missed or repeated event can create inconsistent decisions.  Control   Failure prevented  Application-programming-interface key protection and rotation  Impersonation of an authorised organisation.  Transport Layer Security   Interception or alteration in transit.  Range-based update authority   Operator changing a number it does not manage.  Input and status validation   Corrupt or ambiguous central records.  Rate limits and anomaly monitoring   Abuse, scraping and denial of service.  Audit and reconciliation   Undetected omissions or conflicting feeds.  EXAM TRAP - An application-programming-interface response is not self-executing regulation. The receiving institution must interpret it lawfully and proportionately within its own decision controls.

NCC Promotion Exam - Controlled Teaching Expansion v4.0 - Checkpoint 5   Page 224  LEVEL 10 APPLICATION DRILLS  Scenario 1 - Ported number becomes unreachable  The subscriber can call out after porting but callers on two networks hear 'number not assigned'. NCC should verify central port completion, recipient activation, per-network routing lookup, signalling traces and propagation timestamps. The asymmetric pattern points to stale routes on specific networks. Direct correction, test all networks, measure outage and determine compensation or enforcement under the applicable rules.  Scenario 2 - Bank account takeover after SIM replacement  Secure the service and preserve the replacement request, agent identity, capture device, location, verification result, maker-checker approval, old-channel notification and equipment/subscription history. Compare the event with identity-risk updates and the bank's authentication decision. Establish whether the cause was impersonation, insider override, system defect or bank reliance on one-time passwords alone; then remedy each responsible control.  Scenario 3 - Operator requests a very large new range  Do not approve from customer projections alone. Confirm licence scope, inventory, utilisation definitions, churn and quarantine, prior forecast accuracy, launch plan, routing capacity and alternatives. Grant proportionately with milestones if justified, or require better utilisation. Record reasons so later applicants receive consistent treatment.  Scenario 4 - Recycled number receives confidential alerts  Verify the reassignment and quarantine history, ensure the new registration is clean, and help contain disclosure. The operator should not disclose the former user's identity to the new holder. Notify relevant relying organisations through lawful channels, examine whether lifecycle status was published correctly and promote stronger re-authentication beyond number possession.  Scenario 5 - 'Normal' identity-risk response  A financial institution argues that a normal response proves ownership. Correct it: the response indicates no relevant adverse status was returned, subject to data currency; it does not prove the presenter is the lawful subscriber. The institution must perform its own identity and transaction-risk controls.  Scenario 6 - Emergency short code fails on one operator  Treat it as urgent public-safety harm. Confirm the code's authoritative assignment, test access across technologies and locations, inspect translations, routes, interconnection and service-platform capacity, direct interim restoration, communicate alternatives and retain evidence for compliance action.

NCC Promotion Exam - Controlled Teaching Expansion v4.0 - Checkpoint 5   Page 225  EXAM TRAPS, MODEL ANSWER AND SELF-CHECK  Trap   Correct position  A number is owned permanently by an operator or subscriber.  It is a nationally administered resource used under regulatory and service rights.  Allocation means every number is active.   Allocation, activation, use and activity are different states.  A prefix always reveals the current network.   Portability can move the number to another serving provider.  The SIM number, phone number and device identity are the same.  MSISDN, IMSI, ICCID and IMEI identify different objects.  Porting is SIM replacement.   Porting changes provider; replacement changes the SIM or profile.  NIN linkage makes fraud impossible.   It strengthens identity assurance but process, insider and downstream risks remain.  A recycled number carries the former user's legal identity.  The current assignment must be clean; lawful history is retained separately.  TIRMS is only a proposal.   It has a consultation history and current official technical implementation evidence.  A normal TIRMS response proves ownership.   It is a status signal, not complete identity proof.  Short code means free service.   Purpose and tariff depend on the applicable assignment and rules.  THE 45-SECOND MODEL ANSWER  Numbering is the regulated logical-address system that lets networks identify and route communications consistently. NCC plans and assigns resources, monitors efficient use and protects interoperability, competition and consumers. Mobile Number Portability allows a subscriber to retain a number while changing provider, so routing must use authoritative current data rather than prefix alone. The public number, network subscriber identity, SIM-card identifier and device identifier are distinct. Subscriber registration and National Identification Number integration link service to verified identity, while controlled recycling removes old current links but preserves lawful history. The Telecom Identity Risk Management System adds time-sensitive number-status signals for operators and approved relying organisations. Effective regulation therefore combines law, routing, identity, cybersecurity, data governance, audit and redress.  SELF-CHECK  •   Can I explain a number without calling it merely an identifier?  •   Can I distinguish plan, allocation, activation and active use?  •   Can I trace a port and diagnose stale routing?  •   Can I distinguish MSISDN, IMSI, ICCID and IMEI in plain English?  •   Can I explain why recycling is necessary and risky?  •   Can I state the layered status of TIRMS accurately?  •   Can I turn a fraud complaint into evidence, containment, remedy and systemic control?
